- to go on foot, spy out, cause to walk
- (Tiphel) to teach to walk

H8638.gloss: a denominative from «07275» in the sense of throwing over; to transfer, i.e. translate:--interpret.

H8639.gloss: from «07290»; a lethargy or (by implication) trance:--deep sleep.

H8640.gloss: of foreign derivation; Tirhakah, a king of Kush:--Tirhakah.
H8640.outline:
Tirhakah = "he searched out the pious: he searched out the waiter"
- king of Ethiopia and Egypt in the time of Sennacherib

H8641.gloss: or trumah (Deut. 12:11) {ter-oo-maw'}; from «07311»; a present (as offered up), especially in sacrifice or as tribute:-- gift, heave offering ((shoulder)), oblation, offered(-ing).
H8641.outline:
- contribution, offering
- a heave offering
- any offering
- an offering to God
- an offering (of grain, money, etc)
- contribution

H8642.outline: - portion, contribution, what belongs to a contribution or attendant or secondary contribution or subdivision

H8643.gloss: from «07321»; clamor, i.e. acclamation of joy or a battle-cry; especially clangor of trumpets, as an alarum:--alarm, blow(- ing) (of, the) (trumpets), joy, jubile, loud noise, rejoicing, shout(-ing), (high, joyful) sound(-ing).
H8643.outline:
- alarm, signal, sound of tempest, shout, shout or blast of war or alarm or joy
- alarm of war, war-cry, battle-cry
- blast (for march)
- shout of joy (with religious impulse)
- shout of joy (in general)

H8644.gloss: from «07322» in the sense of its congener «07495»; a remedy:--medicine.

H8645.gloss: probably from «07329»; a species of tree (apparently from its slenderness), perhaps the cypress:--cypress.
H8645.outline:
- a type of tree
- perhaps the cypress, holm-tree
- meaning very dubious

H8646.gloss: of uncertain derivation; Terach, the father of Abraham; also a place in the Desert:--Tarah, Terah.
H8646.outline:
Terah = "station" n pr m
- the father of Abraham Tarah = "delay" n pr loc
- a station of Israel in the wilderness

H8647.gloss: of uncertain derivation; Tirchanah, an Israelite:--Tirhanah.
H8647.outline:
Tirhanah = "favour"
- a Judaite, son of Caleb by his concubine Maachah

H8648.gloss: (Aramaic) feminine tarteyn {tar-tane'}; corresponding to «08147»; two:--second, + twelve, two.
H8648.outline:
- two
- two (as cardinal number)
- second (as ordinal number)
- two (in combination with other numbers)

H8649.gloss: and tarmuwth {tar-mooth'}; or tarmiyth {tar-meeth'}; from «07411»; fraud:--deceit(-ful), privily.

H8650.gloss: probably for «0766»; a pole (as a mast or flag-staff):--beacon, mast.

H8651.gloss: (Aramaic) corresponding to «08179»; a door; by implication, a palace:--gate mouth.

H8654.gloss: patrial from an unused name meaning gate; a Tirathite or inhabitant of an unknown Tirah:--Tirathite.
H8654.outline:
Tirathites = "men of the gate"
- one of the 3 families of Kenite scribes living at Jabez

H8655.gloss: plural from «07495»; a healer; Teraphim (singular or plural) a family idol:--idols(-atry), images, teraphim.
H8655.outline:
- idolatry, idols, image(s), teraphim, family idol
- a kind of idol used in household shrine or worship

H8656.gloss: from «07521»; delightsomeness; Tirtsah, a place in Palestine; also an Israelitess:--Tirzah.
H8656.outline:
Tirzah = "favourable" n pr f
- one of the 7 daughters of Zelophehad the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh n pr loc
- one of the kingdoms on the west of the Jordan conquered by Joshua and the Israelites
- a Canaanite city, later capital of the northern kingdom of Israel

H8657.gloss: of foreign derivation; Teresh, a eunuch of Xerxes:--Teresh.
H8657.outline:
Teresh = "strictness"
- one of the 2 eunuchs who plotted to kill king Ahasuerus of Persia but whose plot was discovered by Mordecai

H8658.gloss: probably of foreign derivation (compare «08659»); a gem, perhaps the topaz:--beryl.
H8658.outline:
- a precious stone or semi-precious gem
- perhaps a chrysolite, yellow jasper, or other yellow coloured stone

H8659.gloss: probably the same as «08658» (as the region of the stone, or the reverse); Tarshish, a place on the Mediterranean, hence, the ephithet of a merchant vessel (as if for or from that port); also the name of a Persian and of an Israelite:--Tarshish, Tharshish.
H8659.outline:
Tarshish or Tharshish = "yellow jasper" n pr m
- son of Javan
- a Benjamite, son of Bilhan
- one of the wise men close to king Ahasuerus of Persia n pr loc
- a city of the Phoenicians in a distant part of the Mediterranean Sea to which the prophet Jonah was trying to flee
- site unknown but perhaps in Cyprus or Spain
- a city somewhere near and accessible to the Red Sea to which ships constructed at Ezion-geber on the Elanitic Gulf on the Red Sea were to sail

H8660.gloss: of foreign derivation; the title of a Persian deputy or governor:--Tirshatha.
H8660.outline:
- Tirshatha - governor
- a title used by the Persian governor in Judea
- Nehemiah used this title

H8661.gloss: of foreign derivation; Tartan, an Assyrian:--Tartan.
H8661.outline:
- Tartan - field marshal, general, or commander
- a title used by the Assyrian military

H8662.gloss: of foreign derivation; Tartak, a deity of the Avvites:--Tartak.
H8662.outline:
Tartak = "prince of darkness"
- one of the deities of the Avite people of Samaria
- according to tradition, worshipped under the form of an ass

H8663.gloss: from «07722»; a crashing or loud clamor:--crying, noise, shouting, stir.

H8664.gloss: patrial from an unused name meaning recourse; a Tishbite or inhabitant of Tishbeh (in Gilead):--Tishbite.
H8664.outline:
Tishbite = "captivity" n pr loc
- the home of Elijah
- site unknown but maybe the town of Tishbe adj gent
- an inhabitant of Tishbe or Tishbi or Tesheb
- site unknown and name uncertain

H8665.outline: - woven work, checkered material, chequered or plaited work

H8666.gloss: or tshubah {tesh-oo-baw'}; from «07725»; a recurrence (of time or place); a reply (as returned):--answer, be expired, return.
H8666.outline:
- a recurrence, an answer, return
- return
- completion of a year, return of a year
- at the return (construct)
- answer, reply

H8667.gloss: from «07760»; a deposit, i.e. pledging:--+ fellowship.

H8668.gloss: or tshuah {tesh-oo-aw'}; from «07768» in the sense of «03467»; rescue (literal or figurative, pers., national or spir.):-- deliverance, help, safety, salvation, victory.
H8668.outline:
- salvation, deliverance
- deliverance (usually by God through human agency)
- salvation (spiritual in sense)

H8669.gloss: from «07783» in the original sense of stretching out after; a longing:--desire.
H8669.outline:
- desire, longing, craving
- of man for woman
- of woman for man
- of beast to devour

H8670.gloss: from «07788» in the sense of arrival; a gift:--present.

H8672.gloss: or (masculine) tishtah {tish-aw'}; perhaps from «08159» through the idea of a turn to the next or full number ten; nine or (ord.) ninth:--nine (+ -teen, + -teenth, -th).
H8672.outline:
- nine, nonad
- nine (as cardinal number)
- ninth (as ordinal number)
- in combination with other numbers

H8674.gloss: of foreign derivation; Tattenai, a Persian:--Tatnai.
H8674.outline:
Tatnai = "gift"
- a Persian governor in Syria who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem

G1.gloss: of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first: --Alpha. Often used (usually an, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from «427») in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of «260»).
G1.outline:
- first letter of Greek alphabet
- Christ is the Alpha to indicate that he is the beginning and the end

G2.gloss: of Hebrew origin («0175»); Aaron, the brother of Moses:--Aaron.
G2.outline:
Aaron = "light-bringer"
- the brother of Moses, the first high priest of Israel and head of the whole priestly order

G3.gloss: of Hebrew origin («011»); a destroying angel:--Abaddon.
G3.outline:
Abaddon = "destruction"
- ruin
- destruction
- the place of destruction
- the name of the angel-prince of the infernal regions, the minister of death and the author of havoc on the earth

G4.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «922»; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome:--from being burdensome.
G4.outline:
- not burdensome
- not heavy
- light without weight

G5.gloss: of Chaldee origin («02»); father as a vocative:--Abba.
G5.outline:
Abba = "father"
- father, customary title used of God in prayer. Whenever it occurs in the New Testament it has the Greek interpretation joined to it, that is apparently to be explained by the fact that the Chaldee "ABBA" through frequent use in prayer, gradually acquired the nature of a most sacred proper name, to which the Greek speaking Jews added the name from their own tongue.

G6.gloss: of Hebrew origin («01893»); Abel, the son of Adam:--Abel.
G6.outline:
Abel = "vanity (that is: transitory)"
- the second son of Adam, murdered by his brother Cain

G7.gloss: of Hebrew origin («029»); Abijah, the name of two Israelites:--Abia.
G7.outline:
Abijah = "my father is Jah (Jehovah)"
- a priest, the head of a priestly family from whom when David divided the priests into 24 classes, Abia was the 8th order
- son and successor to Rehoboam on the throne of Judah

G8.gloss: of Hebrew origin («054»); Abiathar, an Israelite:--Abiathar.
G8.outline:
Abiathar = "father of abundance"
- the name of a high priest

G9.gloss: of foreign origin (compare «058»); Abilene, a region of Syria:--Abilene.
G9.outline:
Abilene = "grassy meadow"
- a region of Syria between Lebanon and Hermon towards Phoenicia, 18 miles (29 km) from Damascus and 37 miles (60 km) from Heliopolis

G10.gloss: of Hebrew origin («031»); Abihud, an Israelite:--Abiud.
G10.outline:
Abiud = "my father is majesty"
- the son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin (1 Ch. 8:

G11.gloss: of Hebrew origin («085»); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch:--Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)
G11.outline:
Abraham = "father of a multitude"
- the son of Terah and the founder of the Jewish nation

G12.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a variation of «1037»; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss":--deep, (bottomless) pit.
G12.outline:
- bottomless
- unbounded
- the abyss
- the pit
- the immeasurable depth
- of Orcus, a very deep gulf or chasm in the lowest parts of the earth used as the common receptacle of the dead and especially as the abode of demons

G13.gloss: of Hebrew origin (compare «02285»); Agabus, an Israelite:--Agabus.

G14.gloss: from «18» and «2041»; to work good:--do good.
G14.outline: - to work good, to do good, to do well, act rightly

G15.gloss: from «17»; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty):--(when) do good (well).
G15.outline:
- to do good, do something which profits others
- to be a good help to someone
- to do someone a favour
- to benefit
- to do well, do right

G16.outline: - a course of right action, well doing, virtue

G17.gloss: from «18» and «4160»; a well-doer, i.e. virtuous:--them that do well.

G18.gloss: a primary word; "good" (in any sense, often as noun):--benefit, good(-s, things), well. Compare «2570».
G18.outline:
- of good constitution or nature
- useful, salutary
- good, pleasant, agreeable, joyful, happy
- excellent, distinguished
- upright, honourable

G19.gloss: from «18»; goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence:--goodness.
G19.outline: - uprightness of heart and life, goodness, kindness

G21.gloss: from agan (much) and «242»; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult:--be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly).
G21.outline: - to exult, rejoice exceedingly, be exceeding glad

G22.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1062»; unmarried:--unmarried.

G23.gloss: from agan (much) and achthos (grief; akin to the base of «43»); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant:--be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation.
G23.outline: - to be indignant, moved with indignation, be very displeased

G25.gloss: perhaps from agan (much) (or compare «5689»); to love (in a social or moral sense):--(be-)love(-ed). Compare «5368».
G25.outline:
- of persons
- to welcome, to entertain, to be fond of, to love dearly
- of things
- to be well pleased, to be contented at or with a thing

G26.gloss: from «25»; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast:--(feast of) charity(-ably), dear, love.
G26.outline:
- brotherly love, affection, good will, love, benevolence
- love feasts

G27.outline: - beloved, esteemed, dear, favourite, worthy of love

G28.gloss: of Hebrew origin («01904»); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham:--Hagar.
G28.outline:
Hagar = "flight"
- Abraham's concubine and mother to Ishmael

G29.gloss: of foreign origin (compare «0104»); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service:--compel (to go).
G29.outline: - to employ a courier, dispatch a mounted messenger, press into public service, compel to go

G30.gloss: from aggos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of «43»); a receptacle:--vessel.
G30.outline: - a vessel, receptacle, a pail, a reservoir

G31.gloss: from «32»; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept:--message.
G31.outline:
- message, announcement, news
- a proclamation, command, order

G32.gloss: from aggello (probably derived from «71»; compare «34») (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor:--angel, messenger.
G32.outline: - a messenger, envoy, one who is sent, an angel, a messenger from God

G33.gloss: imperative of «71»; properly, lead, i.e. come on:--go to.

G34.outline: - herd or oxen or cattle, a herd or company

G35.gloss: from «1» (as negative particle) and «1075»; unregistered as to birth:--without descent.
G35.outline: - one whose descent there is no record of, without genealogy

G36.gloss: from «1» (as negative particle) and «1085»; properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble:--base things.
G36.outline: - ignoble, coward, mean, base, of no family, that is: low born

G37.gloss: from «40»; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate:--hallow, be holy, sanctify.
G37.outline:
- to render or acknowledge, or to be venerable or hallow
- to separate from profane things and dedicate to God
- consecrate things to God
- dedicate people to God
- to purify
- to cleanse externally
- to purify by expiation: free from the guilt of sin
- to purify internally by renewing of the soul

G38.gloss: from «37»; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier:--holiness, sanctification.
G38.outline:
- consecration, purification
- the effect of consecration
- sanctification of heart and life

G39.gloss: neuter of «40»; a sacred thing (i.e. spot):--holiest (of all), holy place, sanctuary.
G39.outline:
- reverend, worthy of veneration
- of things which on account of some connection with God possess a certain distinction and claim to reverence, as places sacred to God which are not to be profaned
- of persons whose services God employs, for example, apostles
- set apart for God, to be as it were, exclusively his
- services and offerings
- prepared for God with solemn rite, pure, clean
- in a moral sense, pure sinless upright holy

G40.gloss: from hagos (an awful thing) (compare «53», «2282»); sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated):--(most) holy (one, thing), saint.

G41.outline:
- sanctity
- in a moral sense: holiness

G43.gloss: from agkos (a bend, "ache"); an arm (as curved):--arm.
G43.outline:
- the curve or inner angle of the arm, the bent arm
- anything closely enfolding, as the arms of the sea, etc.

G44.gloss: from the same as «43»; a hook (as bent):--hook.
G44.outline: - a fishing hook, a small hook

G45.gloss: from the same as «43»; an "anchor" (as crooked):--anchor.
G45.outline:
- an anchor
- metaph. any stay or safeguard

G46.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and the same as «1102»; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth):--new.

G48.gloss: from «53»; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally):--purify (self).
G48.outline:
- ceremonially
- to make pure, purify, cleanse
- morally

G49.gloss: from «48»; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration:--purification.

G50.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «3539»; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination):--(be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown.
G50.outline:
- to be ignorant, not to know
- not to understand, unknown
- to err or sin through mistake, to be wrong

G51.gloss: from «50»; a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming:--error.
G51.outline: - a sin committed through ignorance or thoughtlessness

G52.outline:
- lack of knowledge, ignorance
- esp. of divine things
- of moral blindness

G53.gloss: from the same as «40»; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect:--chaste, clean, pure.
G53.outline:
- exciting reverence, venerable, sacred
- pure
- pure from carnality, chaste, modest
- pure from every fault, immaculate
- clean

G56.gloss: from «1» (as negative particle) and «1108»; ignorance (properly, the state):--ignorance, not the knowledge.

G57.outline:
- unknown, forgotten
Epimenides, a certain Cretan, came to Athens to stop a plague. Heoffered a sheep on alters the born no name of no god but to the"unknown god". At least one of the alters survived to Paul's day.

G58.gloss: from ageiro (to gather; probably akin to «1453»); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare:--market(-place), street.
G58.outline:
- any assembly, especially of the people
- the place of assembly
- for public debating,
- for elections
- for trials
- for buying and selling
- for all kinds of business
- market place, street

G59.gloss: from «58»; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem:--buy, redeem.
G59.outline:
- to be in the market place, to attend it
- to do business there, buy or sell
- of idle people: to haunt the market place, lounge there

G60.gloss: from «58»; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar:--baser sort, low.
G60.outline:
- in, of or belonging to the market place
- frequenting the market place
- hucksters, petty traffickers, retail dealers
- idlers, loungers, the common sort, low, mean vulgar
- generally, proper to the assembly, suited to forensic speaking, business-like transactions

G61.gloss: from «71»; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish):--draught.
G61.outline:
- a catching, hunting
- that which is taken in hunting, the booty, prey
- of birds or beasts, game
- of fish, a draught or haul

G62.gloss: from «1» (as negative particle) and «1121»; unlettered, i.e. illiterate:--unlearned.

G63.gloss: from «68» and «832» (in the sense of «833»); to camp out:--abide in the field.
G63.outline: - to live in the fields, be under the open sky, even at night

G64.gloss: from «61»; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap:--catch.
G64.outline:
- to hunt, to take by hunting, catch
- metaph. to hunt after, pursue eagerly

G65.gloss: from «66» and «1636»; an oleaster:--olive tree (which is) wild.
G65.outline:
- of or belonging to the oleaster or wild olive
- the oleaster, wild olive tree

G66.gloss: from «68»; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce):--wild, raging.
G66.outline:
- living or growing in the fields or woods
- of animals, wild, savage
- of countries, wild, uncultivated, unreclaimed
- of men and animals in a moral sense, wild savage, fierce
- boorish, rude
- of any violent passion, vehement, furious

G67.gloss: apparently from «66» and «2462»; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods:--Agrippa.
G67.outline:
Agrippa = "Hero like"
- Name of a ruling family in Israel at the time of Christ

G68.gloss: from «71»; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet:--country, farm, piece of ground, land.
G68.outline:
- land
- the field, the country
- a piece of land, bit of tillage
- the farms, country seats, neighbouring hamlets

G69.gloss: ultimately from «1» (as negative particle) and «5258»; to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake:--watch.
G69.outline:
- to be sleepless, keep awake, watch
- to be circumspect, attentive, ready

G70.gloss: from «69»; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake:--watch.

G71.gloss: a primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce:--be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open.
G71.outline:
- to lead, take with one
- to lead by laying hold of, and this way to bring to the point of destination: of an animal
- to lead by accompanying to (into) a place
- to lead with one's self, attach to one's self as an attendant
- to conduct, bring
- to lead away, to a court of justice, magistrate, etc.
- to lead,
- to lead, guide, direct
- to lead through, conduct to: to something
- to move, impel: of forces and influences on the mind
- to pass a day, keep or celebrate a feast, etc.
- to go, depart

G72.gloss: reduplicated from «71»; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living:--manner of life.
G72.outline:
- a leading
- metaph.: conduct
- a conducting, training, education, discipline
- the life led, way or course of life

G73.gloss: from «71»; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety:--conflict, contention, fight, race.
G73.outline:
- an assembly,
- a place of assembly: especially an assembly met to see games
- the place of contest, the arena or stadium
- the assembly of the Greeks at their national games
- hence the contest for a prize at their games
- generally, any struggle or contest
- a battle
- an action at law, trial

G74.gloss: from «73»; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish:--agony.
G74.outline:
- a struggle for victory
- gymnastic exercise, wrestling
- of severe mental struggles and emotions, agony, anguish

G75.gloss: from «73»; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something):--fight, labor fervently, strive.
G75.outline:
- to enter a contest: contend in the gymnastic games
- to contend with adversaries, fight
- metaph. to contend, struggle, with difficulties and dangers
- to endeavour with strenuous zeal, strive: to obtain something

G76.gloss: of Hebrew origin («0121»); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative):--Adam.
G76.outline:
Adam = "the red earth"
- Adam, the first man, the parent of the whole human family

G77.gloss: from «1» (as negative particle); and «1160»; costless, i.e. gratuitous:--without expense.
G77.outline: - without expense, requiring no outlay, costing nothing

G78.gloss: probably of Hebrew origin (compare «05716»); Addi, an Israelite:--Addi.
G78.outline:
Addi = "ornament"
- son of Cosam, and father of Melchi in our Lord's genealogy

G79.gloss: fem of «80»; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically):--sister.
G79.outline:
- a full, own sister
- one connected by the tie of the Christian religion

G80.gloss: from «1» (as a connective particle) and delphus (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like «1»):--brother.
G80.outline:
- a brother, whether born of the same two parents or only of the same father or mother
- having the same national ancestor, belonging to the same people, or countryman
- any fellow or man
- a fellow believer, united to another by the bond of affection
- an associate in employment or office
- brethren in Christ
- his brothers by blood
- all men
- apostles
- Christians, as those who are exalted to the same heavenly place

G81.gloss: from «80»; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity:--brethren, brotherhood.
G81.outline:
- brotherhood, brotherly kindness
- a family of brothers, the brotherhood

G82.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1212»; hidden, figuratively, indistinct:--appear not, uncertain.

G85.gloss: from a derivative of adeo (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress (of mind):--be full of heaviness, be very heavy.
G85.outline:
- to be troubled, great distress or anguish, depressed
This is the strongest of the three Greek words (85, 916,
- inthe NT for depression.

G86.gloss: from «1» (as negative particle) and «1492»; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls:--grave, hell.
G86.outline:
- name Hades or Pluto, the god of the lower regions
- Orcus, the nether world, the realm of the dead
- later use of this word: the grave, death, hell

G87.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «1252»; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial:--without partiality.
G87.outline:
- undistinguished, unintelligible
- without dubiousness, ambiguity or uncertainty

G88.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of «1223» and «3007»; unintermitted, i.e. permanent:--without ceasing, continual.

G89.gloss: adverb from «88»; uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion):--without ceasing.

G90.gloss: from a derivative of a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «1311»; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine):--uncorruptness.

G91.gloss: from «94»; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically):--hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong.
G91.outline:
- absolutely
- to act unjustly or wickedly, to sin,
- to be a criminal, to have violated the laws in some way
- to do wrong
- to do hurt
- transitively
- to do some wrong or sin in some respect
- to wrong some one, act wickedly towards him
- to hurt, damage, harm

G92.gloss: from «91»; a wrong done:--evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong.

G93.gloss: from «94»; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act):--iniquity, unjust, unrighteousness, wrong.
G93.outline:
- injustice, of a judge
- unrighteousness of heart and life
- a deed violating law and justice, act of unrighteousness

G94.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1349»; unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen:--unjust, unrighteous.
G94.outline:
- descriptive of one who violates or has violated justice
- unjust
- unrighteous, sinful
- of one who deals fraudulently with others, deceitful

G96.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1384»; unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally):--castaway, rejected, reprobate.
G96.outline:
- not standing the test, not approved
- properly used of metals and coins
- that which does not prove itself such as it ought
- unfit for, unproved, spurious, reprobate

G97.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle}; and «1388»; undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated:--sincere.
G97.outline:
- guileless
- in things: unmixed, unadulterated, pure
- in persons: without dishonest intent, guileless

G98.gloss: from Adramutteion (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium:--of Adramyttium.
G98.outline:
Adramyttium = "I shall abide in death"
- Adramyttium, a seaport of Mysia

G99.gloss: from Adria (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian):--Adria.
G99.outline:
Adriatic = "without wood"
- Adriatic Sea, Adrias, the sea between Greece and Italy

G100.outline:
- bountiful collection, great abundance
- thickness, ripeness, fulness, esp. of the body

G101.gloss: from «102»; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible:--be impossible.
G101.outline:
- impossible
- not to have strength, power, or ability, to be weak
- can not be done, to be impossible

G102.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1415»; unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible:--could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak.
G102.outline:
- without strength, impotent, powerless, weakly, disabled
- unable to be done, impossible

G103.outline: - to the praise of anyone, to sing

G104.gloss: from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); "ever,"by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly; --always, ever.
G104.outline:
- perpetually, incessantly
- invariably, at any and every time: when according to the circumstances something is or ought to be done again

G105.gloss: from the same as «109»; an eagle (from its wind-like flight):--eagle.
G105.outline:
- an eagle: since eagles do not usually go in quest of carrion, this may to a vulture that resembles an eagle
- an eagle as a standard (Roman Military)

G106.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2219»; unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week:--unleavened (bread).
G106.outline:
- unfermented, free from leaven or yeast
- of the unleavened loaves used in the paschal feast of the Jews
- metaph. free from faults or the "leaven of iniquity"

G107.gloss: of Hebrew origin (compare «05809»); Azor, an Israelite:--Azorigin
G107.outline:
Azor = "helper"
- A son of Eliakim, in the line of our Lord. Mat. 1:13,14.

G108.gloss: of Hebrew origin («0795»); Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in Palestine:--Azotus.
G108.outline:
Ashdod or Azotus = "a stronghold"
- one of the five chief cities of the Philistines, lying between Ashkelon and Jamnia and near the Mediterranean

G109.gloss: from aemi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. respire; by analogy, to blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient):--air. Compare «5594».
G109.outline:
- the air, particularly the lower and denser air as distinguished from the higher and rarer air
- the atmospheric region

G110.gloss: from a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and «2288»; deathlessness:--immortality.

G111.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of themis (statute; from the base of «5087»); illegal; by implication, flagitious:--abominable, unlawful thing.
G111.outline: - contrary to law and justice, prohibited by law, illicit, criminal

G112.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2316»; godless:--without God.
G112.outline:
- without God, knowing and worshipping no God
- denying the gods, esp. the recognised gods of the state
- godless, ungodly
- abandoned by the gods

G113.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «5087» (in the sense of enacting); lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal:--wicked.
G113.outline: - one who breaks through the restraint of law and gratifies his lusts

G114.gloss: from a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «5087»; to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate:--cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject.
G114.outline:
- to do away with, to set aside, disregard
- to thwart the efficacy of anything, nullify, make void, frustrate
- to reject, to refuse, to slight

G115.gloss: from «114»; cancellation (literally or figuratively):--disannulling, put away.

G116.gloss: plural of Athene (the goddess of wisdom, who was reputed to have founded the city); Athenoe, the capitol of Greece:-- Athens.
G116.outline:
Athens = "uncertainty"
- A famous city in Greece, the capital of Attica, and the chief seat of learning and civilisation during the golden period of the history of Greece

G117.gloss: from «116»; an Athenoean or inhabitant of Athenae:--Athenian.
G117.outline: - a person who lives in Athens, an Athenian

G118.gloss: from athlos (a contest in the public lists); to contend in the competitive games:--strive.
G118.outline:
- to engage in a contest, contend in public games, contend for a prize
- to endure, suffer

G119.outline: - to contest, to combat, to strive, struggle, hard trial

G120.gloss: from a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and «2372»; to be spiritless, i.e. disheartened:--be dismayed.
G120.outline: - to be disheartened, dispirited, broken in spirit

G121.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of «5087» (meaning a penalty); not guilty:--innocent.

G122.gloss: from aix (a goat); belonging to a goat:--goat.

G123.gloss: from aisso (to rush) and «251» (in the sense of the sea; a beach (on which the waves dash):--shore.
G123.outline: - the shore of the sea, the beach

G124.gloss: from «125»; an Ægyptian or inhabitant of Ægyptus:--Egyptian.

G125.gloss: of uncertain derivation:--Ægyptus, the land of the Nile:--Egypt.
G125.outline:
Egypt = "double straits"
- a country occupying the northeast angle of Africa
- metaph. Jerusalem, for the Jews persecuting the Christ and his followers, and so to be likened to the Egyptians treating the Jews

G126.gloss: from «104»; everduring (forward and backward, or forward only):--eternal, everlasting.

G127.gloss: perhaps from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1492» (through the idea of downcast eyes); bashfulness, i.e. (towards men), modesty or (towards God) awe:--reverence, shamefacedness.
G127.outline: - a sense of shame or honour, modesty, bashfulness, reverence, regard for others, respect

G128.gloss: from aitho (to scorch) and ops (the face, from «3700»); an Æthiopian (as a blackamoor):--Ethiopian.

G129.gloss: of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred:--blood.

G130.gloss: from «129» and a derivative of «1632»; an effusion of blood:--shedding of blood.

G131.gloss: from «129» and «4482»; to flow blood, i.e. have a hoemorrhage:--diseased with an issue of blood.
G131.outline: - to suffer from a flow of blood, to have a discharge of blood, to lose blood

G132.gloss: of uncertain derivation; Aeneas, an Israelite:--Aeneas.
G132.outline:
Aeneas = "laudable"
- the name of a paralytic cured by Peter at Lydia

G133.gloss: from «134»; a praising (the act), i.e. (specially) a thank(-offering):--praise.

G134.outline:
- to praise, extol, to sing praises in honour to God
- to allow, recommend
- to promise or vow

G135.gloss: from a derivative of «136» (in its primary sense); an obscure saying ("enigma"), i.e. (abstractly) obscureness:--X darkly.
G135.outline:
- an obscure saying, enigma, riddle
- an obscure thing

G136.gloss: apparently a prime word; properly, a story, but used in the sense of «1868»; praise (of God):--praise.
G136.outline:
- a saying, proverb
- praise, laudatory discourse

G137.gloss: of Hebrew origin (a derivative of «5869», place of springs); Ænon, a place in Palestine:--Ænon.
G137.outline:
Aenon meaning "springs"
- the name of a place "near to Salim" at which John baptised

G138.gloss: probably akin to «142»; to take for oneself, i.e. to prefer:--choose. Some of the forms are borrowed from a cognate hellomai hel'-lom-ahee; which is otherwise obsolete.
G138.outline:
- to take for oneself, to prefer, choose
- to choose by vote, elect to office

G139.gloss: from «138»; properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion:--heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect.
G139.outline:
- act of taking, capture: e.g. storming a city
- choosing, choice
- that which is chosen
- a body of men following their own tenets (sect or party)
- of the Sadducees
- of the Pharisees
- of the Christians
- dissensions arising from diversity of opinions and aims

G140.gloss: from a derivative of «138»; to make a choice:--choose.
G140.outline:
- to choose
- to belong to a sect

G141.gloss: from the same as «140»; a schismatic:--heretic (the Greek word itself).
G141.outline:
- fitted or able to take or choose a thing
- schismatic, factious, a follower of a false doctrine
- heretic

G142.gloss: a primary root; to lift up; by implication, to take up or away; figuratively, to raise (the voice), keep in suspense (the mind), specially, to sail away (i.e. weigh anchor); by Hebraism (compare «05375») to expiate sin:--away with, bear (up), carry, lift up, loose, make to doubt, put away, remove, take (away, up).
G142.outline:
- to raise up, elevate, lift up
- to raise from the ground, take up: stones
- to raise upwards, elevate, lift up: the hand
- to draw up: a fish
- to take upon one's self and carry what has been raised up, to bear
- to bear away what has been raised, carry off
- to move from its place
- to take off or away what is attached to anything
- to remove
- to carry off, carry away with one
- to appropriate what is taken
- to take away from another what is his or what is committed to him, to take by force
- to take and apply to any use
- to take from among the living, either by a natural death, or by violence
- cause to cease

G143.gloss: of uncertain derivation; to apprehend (properly, by the senses):--perceive.
G143.outline:
- to perceive
- by the bodily senses
- with the mind, understand

G144.outline:
- perception, not only by the senses but by the intellect
- cognition, discernment
- of moral discernment in ethical matters

G145.gloss: from a derivative of «143»; properly, an organ of perception, i.e. (figuratively) judgment:--senses.
G145.outline: - faculty of the mind for perceiving, understanding, judging

G146.gloss: from «150» and kerdos (gain); sordid:--given to (greedy of) filthy lucre.
G146.outline: - eager for base gain, greedy for money

G147.gloss: adverb from «146»; sordidly:--for filthy lucre's sake.

G148.outline: - foul speaking, low and obscene speech

G149.gloss: neuter of «150»; a shameful thing, i.e. indecorum:--shame.

G150.gloss: from the same as «153»; shameful, i.e. base (specially, venal):--filthy.

G152.gloss: from «153»; shame or disgrace (abstractly or concretely):--dishonesty, shame.
G152.outline:
- the confusion of one who is ashamed of anything, sense of shame
- ignominy, disgrace, dishonour
- a thing to be ashamed of

G153.gloss: from aischos (disfigurement, i.e. disgrace); to feel shame (for oneself):--be ashamed.
G153.outline:
- to disfigure
- to dishonour
- to suffuse with shame, make ashamed, be ashamed

G154.gloss: of uncertain derivation; to ask (in genitive case):--ask, beg, call for, crave, desire, require. Compare «4441».
G154.outline: - to ask, beg, call for, crave, desire, require

G155.gloss: from «154»; a thing asked or (abstractly) an asking:--petition, request, required.

G156.gloss: from the same as «154»; a cause (as if asked for), i.e. (logical) reason (motive, matter), (legal) crime (alleged or proved):--accusation, case, cause, crime, fault, (wh-)ere(-fore).
G156.outline:
- cause, reason
- cause for which one is worthy of punishment, crime
- charge of crime, accusation

G157.gloss: from a derivative of «156»; a thing charged:--complaint.
G157.outline: - to accuse, bring a charge against, complaint

G158.gloss: neuter of «159»; a reason or crime (like «156»):--cause, fault.

G159.gloss: from the same as «154»; causative, i.e. (concretely) a causer:--author.
G159.outline:
- that which is the cause of anything resides, causative, causing
- the author
- of a cause
- of crime or offence

G160.gloss: from a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and «5316» (compare «1810») (meaning non-apparent); unexpected, i.e. (adverbially) suddenly:--sudden, unawares.

G162.outline: - to make captive, take captive, capture

G163.gloss: from «164»; to make captive:--lead away captive, bring into captivity.
G163.outline:
- to lead away captive
- metaph. to capture ones mind, captivate

G164.gloss: from aichme (a spear) and a derivative of the same as «259»; properly, a prisoner of war, i.e. (genitive case) a captive:--captive.

G165.gloss: from the same as «104»; properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity (also past); by implication, the world; specially (Jewish) a Messianic period (present or future):--age, course, eternal, (for) ever(-more), (n-)ever, (beginning of the , while the) world (began, without end). Compare «5550».
G165.outline:
- for ever, an unbroken age, perpetuity of time, eternity
- the worlds, universe
- period of time, age

G166.gloss: from «165»; perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well):--eternal, for ever, everlasting, world (began).
G166.outline:
- without beginning and end, that which always has been and always will be
- without beginning
- without end, never to cease, everlasting

G167.gloss: from «169»; impurity (the quality), physically or morally:--uncleanness.
G167.outline:
- uncleanness
- physical
- in a moral sense: the impurity of lustful, luxurious, profligate living
- of impure motives

G169.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of «2508» (meaning cleansed); impure (ceremonially, morally (lewd) or specially, (demonic)):--foul, unclean.
G169.outline:
- not cleansed, unclean
- in a ceremonial sense: that which must be abstained from according to the levitical law
- in a moral sense: unclean in thought and life

G170.gloss: from a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and «2540» (meaning unseasonable); to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. to fail of a proper occasion:--lack opportunity.

G171.gloss: adverb from the same as «170»; inopportunely:--out of season.

G172.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2556»; not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting:--harmless, simple.
G172.outline:
- without guile or fraud, harmless, free from guilt
- fearing no evil from others, distrusting no one

G173.gloss: probably from the same as «188»; a thorn:--thorn.
G173.outline:
- thorn, bramble
- bush, brier, a thorny plant

G174.outline: - thorny, woven out of twigs of a thorny plant

G175.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2590»; barren (literally or figuratively):--without fruit, unfruitful.
G175.outline: - metaph. without fruit, barren, not yielding what it ought to yield

G176.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2607»; unblamable:--that cannot be condemned.
G176.outline: - that cannot be condemned, not to be censored

G177.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of «2596» and «2572»; unveiled:--uncovered.

G178.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2632»; without (legal) trial:--uncondemned.

G179.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2647»; indissoluble, i.e. (figuratively) permanent:--endless.

G180.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2664»; unrefraining:--that cannot cease.
G180.outline:
- unable to stop, unceasing
- not quieted, that cannot be quieted

G181.gloss: from «182»; instability, i.e. disorder:--commotion, confusion, tumult.
G181.outline: - instability, a state of disorder, disturbance, confusion

G182.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2525»; inconstant:--unstable.

G183.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2722»; unrestrainable:--unruly.

G184.gloss: of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood; corresponding to «02506» and «01818»); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem:--Aceldama.
G184.outline:
Aceldama = "Field of Blood"
- a field purchased with Judas's betrayal money, located near Jerusalem

G185.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of «2767»; unmixed, i.e. (figuratively) innocent:--harmless, simple.
G185.outline:
- unmixed, pure as in wines or metals
- of the mind, without a mixture of evil, free from guile, innocent, simple

G186.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2827»; not leaning, i.e. (figuratively) firm:--without wavering.

G187.gloss: from the same as «188»; to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature:--be fully ripe.

G188.gloss: accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to ake (a point) and meaning the same; adverbially, just now, i.e. still:--yet.
G188.outline:
- a point
- extremity, climax, acme, highest degree
- the present time

G189.gloss: from «191»; hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard):--audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor.
G189.outline:
- the sense of hearing
- the organ of hearing, the ear
- the thing heard
- instruction, namely oral
- of preaching the gospel
- hearsay, report or rumour

G190.gloss: from «1» (as a particle of union) and keleuthos (a road); properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. to accompany (specially, as a disciple):--follow, reach.
G190.outline:
- to follow one who precedes, join him as his attendant, accompany him
- to join one as a disciple, become or be his disciple
- side with his party

G191.gloss: a primary verb; to hear (in various senses):--give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand.
G191.outline:
- to be endowed with the faculty of hearing, not deaf
- to hear
- to attend to, consider what is or has been said
- to understand, perceive the sense of what is said
- to hear something
- to perceive by the ear what is announced in one's presence
- to get by hearing learn
- a thing comes to one's ears, to find out, learn
- to give ear to a teaching or a teacher
- to comprehend, to understand

G193.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2904»; powerless, i.e. without self-control:--incontinent.

G194.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of «2767»; undiluted:--without mixture.

G195.gloss: from the same as «196»; exactness:--perfect manner.
G195.outline: - exactness, exactest care: in accordance with the strictness of the Mosaic law

G196.gloss: superlative of akribes (a derivative of the same as «206»); most exact:--most straitest.
G196.outline:
- exact, careful
- of the strictest sect: the most precise and rigorous in interpreting the Mosaic law, and in observing even the more minute precepts of the law and tradition

G197.gloss: neuter of the comparative of the same as «196»; (adverbially) more exactly:--more perfect(-ly).

G198.gloss: from the same as «196»; to be exact, i.e. ascertain:--enquire diligently.
G198.outline:
- to know accurately, to do exactly
- to investigate diligently

G199.gloss: adverb from the same as «196»; exactly:--circumspectly, diligently, perfect(-ly).

G200.gloss: apparently from the same as «206»; a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation):--locust.
G200.outline: - a locust, particularly that species which especially infests oriental countries, stripping fields and trees. Numberless swarms of them almost every spring are carried by the wind from Arabia into Palestine, and having devastated that country, migrate to regions farther north, until they perish by falling into the sea. The Orientals accustomed to feed upon locusts, either raw or roasted and seasoned with salt (or prepared in other ways), and the Israelites also were permitted to eat them.

G201.outline: - a place set aside for hearing and deciding cases

G202.gloss: from akroaomai (to listen; apparently an intensive of «191»); a hearer (merely):--hearer.

G203.gloss: from «206» and probably a modified form of posthe (the penis or male sexual organ); the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person:--not circumcised, uncircumcised (with «2192»), uncircumcision.
G203.outline:
- having the foreskin, uncircumcised
- a Gentile
- a condition in which the corrupt desires rooted in the flesh were not yet extinct

G204.gloss: from «206» and «1137»; belonging to the extreme corner:--chief corner.
G204.outline: - placed at an extreme corner, the corner foundation stone

G205.gloss: from «206» and this (a heap); properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty:--spoils.
G205.outline:
- top of the heap, the first fruits
- best of the spoils or crops
- the Greeks customarily selected from the topmost part of the heaps and offered this to the gods

G206.gloss: neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of «188»; the extremity:--one end... other, tip, top, uttermost participle
G206.outline:
- the farthest bounds, uttermost parts, end, highest, extreme
- of the earth
- of heaven

G207.gloss: probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); Akulas, an Israelite:--Aquila.
G207.outline:
Aquila = "an eagle"
- a Jew of Pontus, a tent maker convert to Christ, companion and ally of Paul in propagating Christianity

G208.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «2964»; to invalidate:--disannul, make of none effect.
G208.outline: - to render void, deprive of force and authority

G209.gloss: adverb from a compound of «1» (as a negative particle) and a derivative of «2967»; in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely:--no man forbidding him.

G210.gloss: from «1» (as a negative particle) and «1635»; unwilling:--against the will.
G210.outline: - not of one's own will, unwillingly, against the will

G211.gloss: neuter of alabastros (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone; properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material):--(alabaster) box.
G211.outline:
- a box made of alabaster in which unguents are preserved
The ancients considered alabaster to be the best material inwhich to preserve their ointments. Breaking the box, probablymeans breaking the seal of the box.

G212.gloss: from «213»; braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) self-confidence:--boasting, pride.
G212.outline:
- empty, braggart talk
- an insolent and empty assurance, which trusts in its own power and resources and shamefully despises and violates divine laws and human rights
- an impious and empty presumption which trusts in the stability of earthy things

G214.gloss: from alale ( a shout, "halloo"); to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang:--tinkle, wail.

1. firm
    1. metaph. faithful
  2. verily, amen
    1. at the beginning of a discourse - surely, truly, of a truth
    2. at the end - so it is, so be it, may it be fulfilled. It was a custom, which passed over from the synagogues to the Christian assemblies, that when he who had read or discoursed, had offered up solemn prayer to God, the others responded Amen, and thus made the substance of what was uttered their own.
The word "amen" is a most remarkable word. It was transliterateddirectly from the Hebrew into the Greek of the New Testament, theninto Latin and into English and many other languages, so that it ispractically a universal word. It has been called the best known wordin human speech. The word is directly related -- in fact, almostidentical -- to the Hebrew word for "believe" (amam), or faithful.Thus, it came to mean "sure" or "truly", an expression of absolutetrust and confidence. -- HMM

This word is used in the Gospels to refer to the stone that was infront of the tomb of Jesus. In Palestine, graves were usually in adepression and the stone was rolled down an incline to cover themouth of the tomb. For a small grave, about twenty men were requiredto roll a stone down hill to cover the door of the tomb. The Bibletells us that the stone covering the door of the tomb was a largestone. The women would have needed more men than even a full Romanguard of sixteen men to roll away the stone. This was a major task.

G907.pos:
1. to dip repeatedly, to immerse, to submerge (of vessels sunk)
  2. to cleanse by dipping or submerging, to wash, to make clean with water, to wash one's self, bathe
  3. to overwhelm
Not to be confused with 911, bapto. The clearest example that showsthe meaning of baptizo is a text from the Greek poet and physicianNicander, who lived about 200 B.C. It is a recipe for making picklesand is helpful because it uses both words. Nicander says that inorder to make a pickle, the vegetable should first be 'dipped'(bapto) into boiling water and then 'baptised' (baptizo) in thevinegar solution. Both verbs concern the immersing of vegetables in asolution. But the first is temporary. The second, the act ofbaptising the vegetable, produces a permanent change. When used in the New Testament, this word more often refers to ourunion and identification with Christ than to our water baptism. e.g.Mark 16:16. 'He that believes and is baptised shall be saved'.Christ is saying that mere intellectual assent is not enough. Theremust be a union with him, a real change, like the vegetable to thepickle! Bible Study Magazine, James Montgomery Boice, May 1989.

This was valid Christian baptism, as this was the only baptism the apostles received and it is not recorded anywhere that they were ever rebaptised after Pentecost.
- of Christian baptism; a rite of immersion in water as commanded by Christ, by which one after confessing his sins and professing his faith in Christ, having been born again by the Holy Spirit unto a new life, identifies publicly with the fellowship of Christ and the church.
In Rom. 6:3 Paul states we are "baptised unto death" meaning that weare not only dead to our former ways, but they are buried. To returnto them is as unthinkable for a Christian as for one to dig up a deadcorpse! In Moslem countries a new believer has little trouble withMoslems until he is publicly baptised. It is then, that the Moslems'know he means business, and then the persecution starts. See alsodiscussion of baptism under No. 907.

In the Greek was called Lithostrotos, or the pavement of stones,as the Syrian version renders it: it is thought to be the roomGazith, in which the sanhedrin sat in the temple when they triedcapital causes; and it was so called, because it was paved withsmooth, square hewn stones: "it was in the north part; half of itwas holy, and half of it was common: and it had two doors, one forthat part which was holy, and another for that part that was common;and in that half that was common the sanhedrin sat." So that intothis part of it, and by this door, Pilate, though a Gentile, mightenter. This place, in the language of the Jews, who at that timespoke Syrian, was Gabbatha, from its height, as it should seem;though the Syrian and Persian versions read Gaphiphtha, whichsignifies a fence or enclosure. Mention is made in the Talmud of theupper Gab in the mountain of the house; but whether the same withthis Gabbatha, and whether this is the same with the chamber Gazith,is not certain. The Septuagint uses the same word as John here does,and calls by the same name the pavement of the temple on whichIsraelites fell and worshipped God. (2 Chr. 7:

Since the advice of men skilled in the law was needed in the examination in the causes and the solution of the difficult questions, they were enrolled in the Sanhedrin; and are mentioned in connection with the priests and elders of the people. See a Bible Dictionary for more information on the scribes.

"For" (as used in Acts 2:38 "for the forgiveness...") could have twomeanings. If you saw a poster saying "Jesse James wanted forrobbery", "for" could mean Jesse is wanted so he can commit arobbery, or is wanted because he has committed a robbery. - the name of a royal family that flourished among the Jews in the times of Christ and the Apostles. Herod the Great was the son of Antipater of Idumaea. Appointed king of Judaea B.C. 40 by the Roman Senate at the suggestion of Antony and with the consent of Octavian, he at length overcame the great opposition which the country made to him and took possession of the kingdom B.C. 37; and after the battle of Actium, he was confirmed by Octavian, whose favour he ever enjoyed. He was brave and skilled in war, learned and sagacious; but also extremely suspicious and cruel. Hence he destroyed the entire royal family of Hasmonaeans, put to death many of the Jews that opposed his government, and proceeded to kill even his dearly beloved wife Mariamne of the Hasmonaean line and his two sons she had borne him. By these acts of bloodshed, and especially by his love and imitation of Roman customs and institutions and by the burdensome taxes imposed upon his subjects, he so alienated the Jews that he was unable to regain their favour by his splendid restoration of the temple and other acts of munificence. He died in the 70th year of his age, the 37th year of his reign, the 4th before the Dionysian era. In his closing years John the Baptist and Christ were born; Matthew narrates that he commanded all the male children under two years old in Bethlehem to be slain.
- Herod surnamed "Antipas", was the son of Herod the Great and Malthace, a Samaritan woman. After the death of his father he was appointed by the Romans tetrarch of Galilee and Peraea. His first wife was the daughter of Aretas, king of Arabia; but he subsequently repudiated her and took to himself Herodias, the wife of his brother Herod Philip; and in consequence Aretas, his father-in-law, made war against him and conquered him. He cast John the Baptist into prison because John had rebuked him for this unlawful connection; and afterwards, at the instigation of Herodias, he ordered him to be beheaded. Induced by her, too, he went to Rome to obtain from the emperor the title of king. But in consequence of the accusations brought against him by Herod Agrippa I, Caligula banished him (A.D.
- to Lugdunum in Gaul, where he seems to have died. He was light minded, sensual and vicious.
- Herod Agrippa I was the son of Aristobulus and Berenice, and grandson of Herod the Great. After various changes in fortune, he gained the favour of Caligula and Claudius to such a degree that he gradually obtained the government of all of Palestine, with the title of king. He died at Caesarea, A.D. 44, at the age of 54, in the seventh [or the 4th, reckoning from the extension of his dominions by Claudius] year of his reign, just after having ordered James the apostle, son of Zebedee, to be slain, and Peter to be cast into prison: Acts 12:
- (Herod) Agrippa II, son of Herod Agrippa I. When his father died he was a youth of seventeen. In A.D. 48 he received from Claudius Caesar the government of Chalcis, with the right of appointing the Jewish high priests, together with the care and oversight of the temple at Jerusalem. Four years later Claudius took from him Chalcis and gave him instead a larger domain, of Batanaea, Trachonitis, and Gaulanitis, with the title of king. To those reigns Nero, in A.D. 53, added Tiberias and Taricheae and Peraean Julias, with fourteen neighbouring villages. He is mentioned in Acts 25 and 26. In the Jewish war, although he strove in vain to restrain the fury of the seditious and bellicose populace, he did not desert to the Roman side. After the fall of Jerusalem, he was vested with praetorian rank and kept the kingdom entire until his death, which took place in the third year of the emperor Trajan, [the 73rd year of his life, and the 52nd of his reign] He was the last representative of the Herodian dynasty.

Herodias = "heroic"
