- in Greek mythology the name of the Pythian serpent or dragon that dwelt in the region of Pytho at the foot of Parnassus in Phocis, and was said to have guarded the oracle at Delphi and been slain by Apollo
- a spirit of divination

G4437.gloss: from the same as «4635»; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently:--often(-er).
G4437.outline:
- thick, dense, compact
- in reference to time
- frequently, often, recurring
- vigorously, diligently
- often, more frequently, the oftener

G4438.gloss: from a derivative of the same as «4435»; to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively):--fight.
G4438.outline: - to be a boxer, to box

G4439.gloss: apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively):--gate.
G4439.outline:
- a gate
- of the larger sort
- in the wall of either a city
- a palace
- a town
- the temple
- a prison
- the gates of hell (likened to a vast prison)
- metaph. the access or entrance into any state

G4440.gloss: from «4439»; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule:--gate, porch.
G4440.outline:
- a large gate: of a palace
- the front part of a house, into which one enters through the gate, porch

G4441.gloss: middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from «2065», which properly means a request as a favor; and from «154», which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from «2212», which implies a search for something hidden; and from «1189», which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence):--ask, demand, enquire, understand.
G4441.outline:
- to enquire, ask
- to ascertain, by enquiry

G4442.gloss: a primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning):--fiery, fire.

G4443.outline: - a fire, a pile of burning fuel

G4444.gloss: apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle:--tower.
G4444.outline:
- a tower
- a fortified structure rising to a considerable height, to repel a hostile attack or to enable a watchman to see in every direction

G4445.gloss: from «4443»; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever:--be sick of a fever.
G4445.outline: - to be sick with a fever

G4446.gloss: from «4445»; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever):--fever.

G4447.gloss: from «4443»; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming:--of fire.

G4448.gloss: from «4442»; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust):--burn, fiery, be on fire, try.
G4448.outline:
- to burn with fire, to set on fire, kindle
- to be on fire, to burn
- to be incensed, indignant
- make to glow
- full of fire, fiery, ignited 1b
- of darts filled with inflammable substances and set on fire
- melted by fire and purged of dross

G4449.outline: - to become glowing, grow red, be red

G4450.outline: - having the colour of fire, red

G4451.gloss: from «4448»; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test):--burning, trial.
G4451.outline:
- a burning
- the burning by which metals are roasted and reduced
- by a figure drawn from a refiners fire
- calamities or trials that test the character

G4452.pos:
1. yet, even
  2. used only in compound with words 3369, 3380, 3764, 3768, 4455
G4452.gloss: another form of the base of «4458»; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See «3369», «3380», «3764», «3768», «4455».

G4453.gloss: probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell:--sell, whatever is sold.

G4454.gloss: apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass:--colt.
G4454.outline:
- a colt, the young of a horse
- a young creature
- of a young ass
- an ass's colt

G4455.gloss: from «4452» and «4218»; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time:--at any time, + never (...to any man), + yet, never man.

G4456.gloss: apparently from poros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous):-- blind, harden.
G4456.outline:
- to cover with a thick skin, to harden by covering with a callus
- metaph.
- to make the heart dull
- to grow hard, callous, become dull, lose the power of understanding

G4457.outline:
- the covering with a callus
- obtrusiveness of mental discernment, dulled perception
- the mind of one has been blunted
- of stubbornness, obduracy

G4458.pos: 1. by any means, at all, perhaps
G4458.gloss: adverb from the base of «4225»; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition:--haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See «1513», «3381». Compare «4459».

G4459.gloss: adverb from the base of «4226»; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!:--how, after (by) what manner (means), that. (Occasionally unexpressed in English).

G4460.gloss: of Hebrew origin («7343»); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess:--Rahab. See also «04477».

G4461.gloss: of Hebrew origin (7227 with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor:--Master, Rabbi.
G4461.outline:
- my great one, my honourable sir
- Rabbi, a title used by the Jews to address their teachers (and also honour them when not addressing them)

G4462.outline:
- master, chief, prince
- Rabboni is a title of honour Mary used to address Jesus

G4463.gloss: from «4464»; to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado:--beat (with rods).

G4464.gloss: from the base of «4474»; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty):--rod, sceptre, staff.
G4464.outline:
- a staff, a walking stick, a twig, rod, branch
- a rod with which one is beaten
- a staff
- as used on a journey, or to lean upon, or by shepherds
- when applied to kings
- with a rod of iron, indicates the severest, most rigorous rule
- a royal sceptre

G4465.gloss: from «4464» and «2192»; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner):--serjeant.
G4465.outline:
- one who carries the rods i.e. the fasces
- a lictor, a public official who bore the fasces or staff and other insignia of office before a magistrate

G4466.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07466»); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch:--Ragau.
G4466.outline:
Reu = "associate ye: feed ye"
- one of the ancestors of Christ

G4467.gloss: from a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and «2041»; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime:--lewdness.
G4467.outline: - a piece of knavery, rascality, villainy

G4468.gloss: from the same as «4467»; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity:--mischief.
G4468.outline:
- ease in doing, faculty
- levity or easiness in thinking or acting
- love of a lazy effeminate life
- unscrupulous, cunning, mischief

G4469.gloss: of Chaldee origin (compare «07386»); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification):--Raca.
G4469.outline:
- empty, i.e. a senseless, empty headed man
- a term of reproach used among the Jews in the time of Christ

G4470.gloss: from «4486»; a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth:--cloth.
G4470.outline:
- a piece torn off
- a bit of cloth
- cloth

G4471.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07414»); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine:--Rama.
G4471.outline:
Ramah = "a hill"
- a town of the tribe of Benjamin, situated about 5 miles (8 km) north of Jerusalem on the road to Bethel

G4472.gloss: from a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively):-- sprinkle.
G4472.outline:
- to sprinkle
- to cleanse by sprinkling, hence to purify, cleanse

G4473.outline:
- a sprinkling (purification)
- blood of sprinkling
- i.e. appointed for sprinkling (serving to purify)

G4474.gloss: from a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, "rap"); to slap:--smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare «5180».
G4474.outline:
- to smite with a rod or staff
- to smite in the face with the palm of the hand, to box the ear

G4475.gloss: from «4474»; a slap:--(+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.
G4475.outline:
- a blow with a rod or staff or a scourge
- a blow with the flat of the hand, a slap in the face, box the ear

G4476.gloss: from a primary rhapto (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of «4474» through the idea of puncturing); a needle:-- needle.

G4477.gloss: from the same as «4460»; Rachab, a Canaanitess:--Rachab.

G4478.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07354»); Rachel, the wife of Jacob:--Rachel.
G4478.outline:
Rachel = "ewe or sheep"
- the wife of Jacob

G4479.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07259»); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac:--Rebecca.

G4480.gloss: of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding):--chariot.
G4480.outline: - a chariot, a type of vehicle having four wheels

G4481.gloss: by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin («03594»); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol:--Remphan.
G4481.outline:
Remphan = "the shrunken (as lifeless)"
- the name of an idol worshipped secretly by the Israelites in the wilderness

G4482.gloss: a primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form   rheuo hryoo'-o is used to flow ("run"; as water):--flow.

G4483.gloss: perhaps akin (or identical) with «4482» (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. speak or say:--command, make, say, speak (of). Compare «3004».

G4484.gloss: of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy:--Rhegium.
G4484.outline:
Rhegium = "breach"
- an Italian town situated on the Bruttian coast, just at the southern entrance of the Straits of Messina

G4485.gloss: from «4486»; something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall):--ruin.
G4485.outline:
- that which has been broken or rent asunder
- a fracture, breach, cleft
- rent clothes
- fall, ruin

G4486.gloss: both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi (see in «2608»)) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; «2608» being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and «2352» a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like «3089») or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions:--break (forth), burst, rend, tear.
G4486.outline:
- to rend, burst or break asunder, break up, break through
- to tear in pieces
- to break forth
- into joy, of infants or dumb persons beginning to speak
- to distort, convulse
- of a demon causing convulsions in a man possessed
- to dash down, hurl to the ground (a common occurrence in cases of demon possession and epilepsy)

G4487.gloss: from «4483»; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever:--+ evil, + nothing, saying, word.
G4487.outline:
- that which is or has been uttered by the living voice, thing spoken, word
- any sound produced by the voice and having definite meaning
- speech, discourse
- what one has said
- a series of words joined together into a sentence (a declaration of one's mind made in words)
- an utterance
- a saying of any sort as a message, a narrative 1c
- concerning some occurrence
- subject matter of speech, thing spoken of
- so far forth as it is a matter of narration
- so far as it is a matter of command
- a matter of dispute, case at law

G4488.gloss: probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for «07509»); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite:--Rhesa.
G4488.outline:
Rhesa = "head"
- the son of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of Christ

G4489.gloss: from «4483»; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate:--orator.
G4489.outline:
- a speaker, an orator
- of a forensic orator or advocate

G4490.gloss: adverb from a derivative of «4483»; out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly:--expressly.

G4491.gloss: apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively):--root.
G4491.outline:
- a root
- that which like a root springs from a root, a sprout, shoot
- metaph. offspring, progeny

G4492.outline: - to cause to strike root, to strengthen with roots, to render firm, to fix, establish, cause a person or a thing to be thoroughly grounded

G4493.gloss: from «4496»; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant):--twinkling.
G4493.outline:
- a throw, stroke, beat
- a moment of time

G4494.gloss: from a derivative of «4496» (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves):--toss.
G4494.outline:
- to raise a breeze, put air in motion, whether for the sake of kindling a fire or cooling one's self
- to blow up a fire
- to fan, i.e. cool with a fan
- to toss to and fro, to agitate
- of the wind
- of persons whose mind wavers in uncertainty between hope and fear, between doing and not doing a thing

G4495.gloss: from a derivative of «4496»; to toss up:--cast off.
G4495.outline:
- to cast, throw
- throw down
- to cast forward or before
- to set down (with the suggestion of haste and want of care)
- to throw to the ground, prostrate

G4496.gloss: a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of «4474», through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from «906», which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from teino (see in «1614»), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse:--cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.
G4496.outline:
- to cast, throw
- throw down
- to cast forward or before
- to set down (with the suggestion of haste and want of care)
- to throw to the ground, prostrate

G4497.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07346»); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite:--Roboam.
G4497.outline:
Rehoboam = "enlarger of the people"
- the son of Solomon by an Ammonite princess Naamah

G4498.gloss: probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl:--Rhoda.
G4498.outline:
Rhoda = "rose"
- the name of a certain maid servant

G4499.gloss: probably from rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Rhodes.
G4499.outline:
Rhodes = "rosy"
- a well known island of the Cyclades opposite Caria and Lycia, with a Rhodes as the capital city

G4500.gloss: adverb from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash:--with a great noise.

G4501.gloss: probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively):--sword.
G4501.outline:
- a large sword
- properly a long Thracian javelin, also a kind of long sword wont to be worn on the right shoulder

G4502.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07205»); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite:--Reuben.
G4502.outline:
Reuben = "behold a son"
- Jacob's firstborn child by Leah

G4503.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07327»); Ruth, a Moabitess:--Ruth.
G4503.outline:
Ruth = "a female friend"
- the ancestor of David and of Christ

G4504.gloss: of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian:--Rufus.
G4504.outline:
Rufus = "red"
- name of a certain Christian

G4505.gloss: prolongation from «4506» in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded):--lane, street.
G4505.outline:
- a swing, rush, force, trail, of a body in motion
- a tract of way in a town shut in by buildings on both sides
- a street, a lane

G4506.gloss: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to «4482» (through the idea of a current; compare «4511»); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue:--deliver(-er).
G4506.outline:
- to draw to one's self, to rescue, to deliver
- the deliverer

G4507.outline:
- to make filthy, befoul
- to defile, dishonour
- to make filthy

G4508.gloss: from «4509»; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked:--vile.
G4508.outline:
- to be dirty, grow filthy
- metaph. to be defiled with iniquity

G4509.gloss: of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity:--filth.

G4510.gloss: from «4509»; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally):--be filthy.
G4510.outline:
- to make filthy, defile, soil
- to be filthy (morally)

G4511.gloss: from «4506» in the sense of its congener «4482»; a flux (of blood):--issue.

G4512.gloss: from «4506»; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face):--wrinkle.

G4513.outline:
Latin = "of Rome's strength"
- the language spoken by the Romans

G4514.gloss: from «4516»; Romaean, i.e. Roman (as noun):--Roman, of Rome.
G4514.outline: - a resident of the city of Rome, a Roman citizen

G4515.gloss: adverb from a presumed derivative of «4516»; Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language:--Latin.
G4515.outline:
Latin = "of Rome's strength"
- the language spoken by the Romans

G4516.gloss: from the base of «4517»; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy:--Rome.
G4516.outline:
Rome = "strength"
- the famous capital of the ancient world

G4517.gloss: prolongation from rhoomai (to dart; probably akin to «4506»); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye):--farewell.
G4517.outline:
- to make strong, strengthen
- to be strong, to thrive, prosper
- in the usual formula in closing of a letter, farewell

G4518.gloss: of Chaldee or (7662 with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress:--sabachthani.

G4519.gloss: of Hebrew origin (6635 in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God:--sabaoth.
G4519.outline:
- "Lord of Sabaoth"
- Lord of the armies of Israel, as those who are under the leadership and protection of Jehovah maintain his cause in war

G4520.gloss: from a derivative of «4521»; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven):--rest.
G4520.outline:
- a keeping sabbath
- the blessed rest from toils and troubles looked for in the age to come by the true worshippers of God and true Christians

G4521.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07676»); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications:--sabbath (day), week.
G4521.outline:
- the seventh day of each week which was a sacred festival on which the Israelites were required to abstain from all work
- the institution of the sabbath, the law for keeping holy every seventh day of the week
- a single sabbath, sabbath day
- seven days, a week

G4522.gloss: from a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing:--net.
G4522.outline: - a large fishing net, a drag net

G4523.gloss: probably from «4524»; a Sadducaean (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite:--Sadducee.
G4523.outline:
Sadducees = "the righteous"
- a religious party at the time of Christ among the Jews, who denied that the oral law was a revelation of God to the Israelites, and who deemed the written law alone to be obligatory on the nation, as the divine authority. They denied the following doctrines:
- resurrection of the body
- immortality of the soul
- existence of spirits and angels
- divine predestination, affirmed free will

G4524.gloss: of Hebrew origin («06659»); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite:--Sadoc.
G4524.outline:
Sadoc = "just"
- a descendant of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of Christ

G4525.gloss: akin to «4579»; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb):--move.
G4525.outline:
- to wag the tail
- of dogs
- metaph.
- to flatter, fawn upon
- to move (the mind of one)
- agreeably
- to agitate, disturb, trouble

G4526.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08242»); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief):-- sackcloth.
G4526.outline:
- a sack
- a receptacle for holding or carrying various things, as money, food, etc.
- a course cloth, a dark course stuff made especially from the hair of animals
- a garment of the like material, and clinging to the person like a sack, which was wont to be worn (or drawn over the tunic instead of the cloak or mantle) by mourners, penitents, suppliants and also by those who like the Hebrew prophets, lead an austere life

G4527.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07974»); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch :--Sala.
G4527.outline:
Salah = "sprout"
- the son of Arphaxad, and father of Eber

G4528.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07597»); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite:--Salathiel.
G4528.outline:
Shealtiel = "I have asked of God"
- the son of Jeconiah in the genealogy of Christ

G4529.gloss: probably from «4535» (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus:--Salamis.
G4529.outline:
Salmis = "salt"
- a principal city at the east end of the island of Cyprus

G4530.gloss: probably from the same as «4531»; Salim, a place in Palestine:--Salim.
G4530.outline:
Salim = "peace"
- a well known town 8 miles (11 km) south of Scythopolis

G4531.gloss: from «4535»; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite:--move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.
G4531.outline:
- a motion produced by winds, storms, waves, etc
- to agitate or shake
- to cause to totter
- to shake thoroughly, of a measure filled by shaking its contents together
- to shake down, overthrow
- to cast down from one's (secure and happy) state
- to move, agitate the mind, to disturb one

G4532.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08004»); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine:--Salem.
G4532.outline:
Salem = "peace"
- the place where Melchizedek was king and thought to be the ancient name of Jerusalem

G4533.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08012»); Salmon, an Israelite:--Salmon.
G4533.outline:
Salmon = "raiment: a garment"
- the father of Boaz in the genealogy of Christ

G4534.gloss: perhaps of similar origin to «4529»; Salmone, a place in Crete:--Salmone.
G4534.outline:
Salmone = "clothed"
- a bold promontory on the east point of the island of Crete

G4535.gloss: probably from the base of «4525»; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow:--wave.
G4535.outline: - the tossing or swell of the sea

G4536.gloss: perhaps from «4535» (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet:--trump(-et).

G4537.gloss: from «4536»; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively):--(which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).

G4539.gloss: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from «07965»); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess:--Salome.
G4539.outline:
Salome = "peaceful"
- the wife of Zebedee and the mother of the apostle James the elder and John

G4540.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08111»); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine:--Samaria.
G4540.outline:
Samaria = "guardianship"
- a territory in Palestine, which had Samaria as its capital

G4541.gloss: from «4540»; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria:--Samaritan.
G4541.outline:
- a Samaritan,
- an inhabitant of the city of Samaria
- an inhabitant of the region of Samaria

G4542.gloss: feminine of «4541»; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria:--of Samaria.

G4543.gloss: from «4544» and Thraike (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean:--Samothracia.
G4543.outline:
Samothracia = "a sign of rags"
- an island on the Aegean Sea, about 38 Miles (60 km) from the coast of Thrace at the mouth of the river Hebrus

G4544.gloss: of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Samos.
G4544.outline:
Samos = "a sandy bluff"
- an island off that part of Asia Minor where Ionia touches Caria

G4545.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08050»); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite:--Samuel.
G4545.outline:
Samuel = "his name is of God"
- the son of Elkanah and Hannah, the last of the judges, a distinguished prophet, and a founder of the prophetic order, he gave the Jews there first kings, Saul, David

G4546.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08123»); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite:--Samson.
G4546.outline:
Samson = "like the sun"
- a famous judge of Israel renowned for his physical strength

G4547.gloss: neuter of a derivative of sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad:--sandal.
G4547.outline: - a sandal, a sole made of wood or leather, covering the bottom of the foot and bound on with thongs

G4549.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07586»); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul. Compare «4569».
G4549.outline:
Saul = "desired"
- the Jewish name of the apostle Paul
- the son of Kish and the first king of Israel

G4550.gloss: from «4595»; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):--bad, corrupt. Compare «4190».
G4550.outline:
- rotten, putrefied
- corrupted by one and no longer fit for use, worn out
- of poor quality, bad, unfit for use, worthless

G4551.outline:
Sapphira = "a sapphire"
- the wife of Ananias

G4552.gloss: of Hebrew origin («05601»); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem:--sapphire.

G4553.gloss: apparently of Hebrew origin («08276»); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work:--basket.
G4553.outline:
- a braided rope, a band
- a basket, a basket made of ropes, a hamper

G4554.gloss: plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor:--Sardis.
G4554.outline:
Sardis = "red ones"
- a luxurious city in Asia Minor, the capital of Lydia

G4555.gloss: from the same as «4556»; sardine (3037 being implied), i.e. a gem, so called:--sardine.
G4555.outline: - a sardius, a precious stone of which there are two types, the former is called a carnelian (because flesh coloured) and the latter a sard

G4556.gloss: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called:--sardius.
G4556.outline: - a sardius, a precious stone of which there are two types, the former is called a carnelian (because flesh coloured) and the latter a sard

G4557.gloss: from the base of «4556» and onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called:-- sardonyx.
G4557.outline: - a sardonyx, a precious stone marked by the red colours of the carnelian (sard) and the white of the onyx

G4558.gloss: of Hebrew origin («06886»); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine:--Sarepta.
G4558.outline:
Sarepta = "smelting"
- the Greek name for Zarephath, a Phoenician town between Tyre and Sidon, but nearer Sidon

G4559.gloss: from «4561»; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate:--carnal, fleshly.
G4559.outline:
- fleshly, carnal
- having the nature of flesh, i.e. under the control of the animal appetites
- governed by mere human nature not by the Spirit of God
- having its seat in the animal nature or aroused by the animal nature
- human: with the included idea of depravity
- pertaining to the flesh
- to the body: related to birth, linage, etc

G4560.gloss: from «4561»; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft:--fleshly.
G4560.outline:
- fleshly, consisting of flesh, composed of flesh
- pertaining to the body (as earthly and perishable material)
- wholly given up to the flesh, rooted in the flesh as it were

G4561.gloss: probably from the base of «4563»; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such):--carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly).
G4561.outline:
- flesh (the soft substance of the living body, which covers the bones and is permeated with blood) of both man and beasts
- the body
- the body of a man
- used of natural or physical origin, generation or relationship
- born of natural generation
- the sensuous nature of man, "the animal nature"
- without any suggestion of depravity
- the animal nature with cravings which incite to sin
- the physical nature of man as subject to suffering
- a living creature (because possessed of a body of flesh) whether man or beast
- the flesh, denotes mere human nature, the earthly nature of man apart from divine influence, and therefore prone to sin and opposed to God

G4562.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08286»); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch:--Saruch.
G4562.outline:
Serug = "intertwined"
- the son of Reu in the genealogy of Christ

G4563.gloss: from a derivative of sairo (to brush off; akin to «4951»); meaning a broom; to sweep:--sweep.

G4564.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08283»); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham:--Sara, Sarah.

G4565.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08289»); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine:--Saron.
G4565.outline:
Sharon = "plain or level"
- a level region extending from Caesarea of Palestine as far as Joppa, abounding in good pasture and famous for its fertility

G4566.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07854»); Satan, i.e. the devil:--Satan. Compare «4567».
G4566.outline:
- adversary (one who opposes another in purpose or act), the name given to
- the prince of evil spirits, the inveterate adversary of God and Christ
- he incites apostasy from God and to sin
- circumventing men by his wiles
- the worshippers of idols are said to be under his control
- by his demons he is able to take possession of men and inflict them with diseases
- by God's assistance he is overcome
- on Christ's return from heaven he will be bound with chains for a thousand years, but when the thousand years are finished he will walk the earth in yet greater power, but shortly after will be given over to eternal punishment
- a Satan-like man

G4567.gloss: of Chaldee origin corresponding to «04566» (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil:--Satan.
G4567.outline:
- adversary (one who opposes another in purpose or act), the name given to
- the prince of evil spirits, the inveterate adversary of God and Christ
- he incites apostasy from God and to sin
- circumventing men by his wiles
- the worshippers of idols are said to be under his control
- by his demons he is able to take possession of men and inflict them with diseases
- by God's assistance he is overcome
- on Christ's return from heaven he will be bound with chains for a thousand years, but when the thousand years are finished he will walk the earth in yet greater power, but shortly after will be given over to eternal punishment
- a Satan-like man

G4568.gloss: of Hebrew origin («05429»); a certain measure for things dry:--measure.
G4568.outline: - a kind of dry measure, 3 gallons (14 litres)

G4569.gloss: of Hebrew origin, the same as «4549»; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul.
G4569.outline:
Saul = "desired"
- the Jewish name of the apostle Paul

G4570.gloss: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively):--go out, quench.
G4570.outline:
- to extinguish, quench
- of fire or things on fire
- to be quenched, to go out
- metaph. to quench, to suppress, stifle
- of divine influence

G4571.gloss: accusative case singular of «4771»; thee:--thee, thou, × thy house.

G4572.gloss: sautoi  sow-to',  and  sauton  sow-ton',  respectively of (with, to) thyself:--thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).

G4573.gloss: middle voice from a derivative of «4576»; to venerate, i.e. adore:--worship.
G4573.outline:
- to fear, be afraid
- to honour religiously, to worship

G4574.gloss: from «4573»; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc):--devotion, that is worshipped.
G4574.outline:
- whatever is religiously honoured, an object of worship
- of temples, altars, statues, idolatrous images

G4575.gloss: from «4573»; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial:--Augustus(-').
G4575.outline:
- reverend, venerable
- the title of the Roman emperors
- Augustan, i,e, taking its name from the emperor
- a title of honour which used to be given certain legions, or cohorts, or battalions, "for valour"

G4576.gloss: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore:--devout, religious, worship.

G4577.gloss: probably from «4951» through its congener eiro (to fasten; akin to «138»); a chain (as binding or drawing):--chain.
G4577.outline:
- a line, a rope
- a chain

G4578.gloss: from «4579»; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake:--earthquake, tempest.
G4578.outline:
- a shaking, a commotion
- a tempest
- an earthquake

G4579.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern):--move, quake, shake.
G4579.outline:
- to shake, agitate, cause to tremble
- of men, to be thrown into a tremor, to quake for fear
- metaph. to agitate the mind

G4580.gloss: of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian:--Secundus.

G4581.gloss: from Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria:--Seleucia.
G4581.outline:
Seleucia = "white light"
- a city of Syria near the mouth of the Orontes, about 16 miles (25 km) from Antioch

G4582.gloss: from selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of «138», through the idea of attractiveness); the moon:--moon.

G4583.gloss: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of «4582»; to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy:--be a lunatic.
G4583.outline:
- to be moon-struck or lunatic
- to be epileptic
- epilepsy being supposed to return and increase with the increase of the moon. This meaning is doubtful as the Greeks knew nothing of epilepsy.

G4584.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08096»); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite:--Semei.
G4584.outline:
Shimei = "harkeners: my report"
- the father of Mattathias in the genealogy of Christ

G4585.gloss: probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour:--fine flour.

G4586.outline:
- august, venerable, reverend
- to be venerated for character, honourable
- of persons
- of deeds

G4587.outline:
- the characteristic of a thing or person which entitles to reverence and respect, dignity, majesty, sanctity
- honour, purity

G4588.gloss: of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman:--Sergius.
G4588.outline:
Sergius = "earth-born: born a wonder"
- surnamed Paulus, a deputy or proconsul of Cyprus and converted to Christianity by Paul

G4589.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08352»); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch:--Seth.
G4589.outline:
Seth = "compensation"
- the third son of Adam and the father of Enos

G4590.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08035»); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch:-- Sem.
G4590.outline:
Shem meaning "name"
- the eldest son of Noah

G4591.gloss: from sema (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate:--signify.
G4591.outline:
- to give a sign, to signify, indicate
- to make known

G4592.gloss: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of «4591»; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally:--miracle, sign, token, wonder.
G4592.outline:
- a sign, mark, token
- that by which a person or a thing is distinguished from others and is known
- a sign, prodigy, portent, i.e. an unusual occurrence, transcending the common course of nature
- of signs portending remarkable events soon to happen
- of miracles and wonders by which God authenticates the men sent by him, or by which men prove that the cause they are pleading is God's

G4593.gloss: from «4592»; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance):--note.
G4593.outline:
- to mark, to note, distinguish by marking
- to mark or note for one's self

G4594.gloss: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article «3588»  (t changed to s) and «2250»; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto):--this (to-)day.
G4594.outline:
- this (very) day)
- what has happened today

G4595.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish:--be corrupted.
G4595.outline:
- to make corrupt, to destroy
- to become corrupt, corrupted, rotten

G4596.gloss: from Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric):--silk.
G4596.outline:
- made of silk
- silk, i.e. the fabric, silken garments

G4597.gloss: apparently of Hebrew origin («05580»); a moth:--moth.

G4598.gloss: from «4597» and a derivative of «977»; moth-eaten:--motheaten.

G4599.gloss: from sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of «2476»); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power):--strengthen.
G4599.outline:
- to make strong, strengthen
- of one's soul

G4600.gloss: of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face:--cheek.

G4601.gloss: from «4602»; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively):--keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.
G4601.outline:
- to keep silence, hold one's peace
- to be kept in silence, be concealed

G4602.gloss: apparently from sizo (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence:--silence. Compare «4623».

G4605.gloss: of Hebrew origin («06721»); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine:--Sidon.
G4605.outline:
Sidon or Zidon = "hunting"
- an ancient and wealthy city of Phoenicia, on the east coast of the Mediterranean Sea, less than 20 miles (30 km) north of Tyre

G4606.gloss: from «4605»; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon:--of Sidon.
G4606.outline: - an inhabitant of Sidon, a Sidonian

G4607.gloss: of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans):--murderer. Compare «5406».
G4607.outline:
- an assassin
- one who carries a dagger or short sword under his clothing, that he may kill secretly and treacherously any one he wishes to
- a cutthroat

G4608.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07941»); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor:--strong drink.
G4608.outline: - strong drink, an intoxicating beverage, different from wine; it was a artificial product, made of a mixture of sweet ingredients, whether derived from grain and vegetables, or from the juice of fruits (dates), or a decoction of honey

G4609.outline:
Silas = "woody"
- a Roman citizen, the companion of the apostle Paul on several of his missionary journeys

G4610.gloss: of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian:--Silvanus. Compare «4609».
G4610.outline:
Silas = "woody"
- a Roman citizen, the companion of the apostle Paul on several of his missionary journeys

G4611.gloss: of Hebrew origin («07975»); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem:--Siloam.
G4611.outline:
Siloam = "sent"
- the Pool of Siloam, a fountain of water in Jerusalem, also called Shiloah in Isa. 8:
- the Tower of Siloam, may have been a tower near or over the Pool of Siloam, which fell down killing 18 men; very likely they were purifying themselves. (Gill)

G4612.gloss: of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron):--apron.
G4612.outline: - a narrow apron, or linen covering, which workmen and servants were accustomed to wear

G4613.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08095»); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites:--Simon. Compare «4826».
G4613.outline:
Peter = "a rock or stone"
- Peter was one of the apostles
- Simon called Zelotes or the Kanaites
- Simon, father of Judas who betrayed Jesus.
- Simon Magus, the Samaritan wizard
- Simon the tanner, Ac.
- Simon the Pharisee, Luke 7:40-
- Simon of Cyrene who carried the cross of Christ
- Simon the cousin of Jesus, the son of Cleophas
- Simon the leper, so called to distinguish him from others of the same name

G4614.gloss: of Hebrew origin («05514»); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia:--Sina.
G4614.outline:
Sinai = "thorny"
- a mountain or rather a mountainous region in the peninsula of Arabia Petraea, made famous by the giving of the Mosaic law

G4615.gloss: perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant):--mustard.
G4615.outline: - mustard, the name of a plant which in oriental countries grows from a very small seed and attains to the height of a tree, 10 feet (3 m) and more; hence a very small quantity of a thing is likened to a mustard seed, and also a thing which grows to a remarkable size

G4616.gloss: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it):--(fine) linen (cloth).
G4616.outline:
- linen cloth, esp. that which was fine and costly, in which the bodies of the dead were wrapped
- thing made of fine cloth
- of a light and loose garment worn at night over a naked body

G4617.outline:
- to sift, shake in a sieve
- fig. by inward agitation to try one's faith to the verge of overthrow

G4618.gloss: from a derivative of «4621»; grain-fed, i.e. fattened:--fatted.

G4619.gloss: from a derivative of «4621»; grained, i.e. fatted:--fatling.

G4620.gloss: from «4621» and «3358»; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food):--portion of meat.

G4621.gloss: of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat:--corn, wheat.

G4622.gloss: of Hebrew origin («06726»); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant):--Sion.
G4622.outline:
Sion or Zion = "a parched place"
- the hill on which the higher and more ancient part of Jerusalem was built
- the southwestern most and highest of the hills on which the city was built
- often used of the entire city of Jerusalem
- since Jerusalem because the temple stood there, was called the dwelling place of God

G4623.gloss: from siope (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from «4602», which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water):--dumb, (hold) peace.
G4623.outline:
- to be silent, hold one's peace
- used of one's silence because dumb
- metaph. of a calm, quiet sea

G4624.gloss: from «4625»; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure):--(make to) offend.
G4624.outline:
- to put a stumbling block or impediment in the way, upon which another may trip and fall, metaph. to offend
- to entice to sin
- to cause a person to begin to distrust and desert one whom he ought to trust and obey
- to cause to fall away
- to be offended in one, i.e. to see in another what I disapprove of and what hinders me from acknowledging his authority
- to cause one to judge unfavourably or unjustly of another
- since one who stumbles or whose foot gets entangled feels annoyed
- to cause one displeasure at a thing
- to make indignant
- to be displeased, indignant

G4625.gloss: ("scandal;" probably from a derivative of «2578»; a  trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin):--occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.
G4625.outline:
- the movable stick or trigger of a trap, a trap stick
- a trap, snare
- any impediment placed in the way and causing one to stumble or fall, (a stumbling block, occasion of stumbling) i.e. a rock which is a cause of stumbling
- fig. applied to Jesus Christ, whose person and career were so contrary to the expectations of the Jews concerning the Messiah, that they rejected him and by their obstinacy made shipwreck of their salvation
- any person or thing by which one is (entrapped) drawn into error or sin

G4626.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to dig:--dig.

G4627.gloss: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing):--boat.
G4627.outline:
- anything dug out, hollow vessel, trough, tray, tub
- of a boat

G4628.gloss: apparently from skello (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank):--leg.
G4628.outline: - the leg, from the hip to the toes inclusive

G4629.gloss: from a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of «4649» through the idea of noticeableness); clothing:--raiment.

G4630.gloss: apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scoevus), an Israelite:--Sceva.
G4630.outline:
Sceva = "mind reader"
- a certain chief priest residing at Ephesus

G4631.outline:
- any apparatus, equipment, or furniture
- of the utensils or tackling of a ship

G4632.gloss: of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively (specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband)):--goods, sail, stuff, vessel.
G4632.outline:
- a vessel
- an implement
- in the plural
- household utensils, domestic gear
- the tackle and armament of vessels, used specifically of sails and ropes
- metaph.
- a man of quality, a chosen instrument
- in a bad sense, an assistant in accomplishing an evil deed
"Vessel" was a common Greek metaphor for "body" since Greeks thoughtof souls living temporarily in bodies.

G4633.gloss: apparently akin to «4632» and «4639»; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively):--habitation, tabernacle.
G4633.outline:
- tent, tabernacle, (made of green boughs, or skins or other materials)
- of that well known movable temple of God after the pattern of which the temple at Jerusalem was built

G4634.gloss: from «4636» and «4078»; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes):--tabernacles.
G4634.outline:
- the construction of a tabernacle or tabernacles
- the feast of tabernacles; this festival was observed by the Jews yearly for seven days, beginning with the 15th of the month Tisri (approx. our Oct.) partly to perpetuate the memory of the time when their ancestors after leaving Egypt dwelt in tents on their way through the Arabian desert, and partly as a season of festivity and joy on the completion of the harvest and the vintage (the festival of ingatherings) In celebrating the festival the Jews were accustomed to construct booths of the leafy branches of trees, -- either on the roofs or in the courts of their dwellings, or in the streets and squares, and to adorn them with flowers and fruits of all kinds -- under which, throughout the period of the festival, they feasted and gave themselves up to rejoicing.

G4635.gloss: from «4633» and «4160»; a manufacturer of tents:--tent-maker.
G4635.outline:
- a tentmaker
- one that makes small portable tents, of leather or cloth of goat's hair or linen, for the use of travellers

G4636.gloss: from «4633»; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit):--tabernacle.
G4636.outline:
- a tabernacle, a tent
- metaph. of the human body, in which the soul dwells as in a tent, and which is taken down at death

G4637.gloss: from «4636»; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion):-- dwell.
G4637.outline:
- to fix one's tabernacle, have one's tabernacle, abide (or live) in a tabernacle (or tent), tabernacle
- to dwell

G4638.gloss: from «4637»; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul):-- tabernacle.
G4638.outline:
- a tent, a tabernacle
- of the temple as God's habitation
- of the tabernacle of the covenant
- metaph. of the human body as the dwelling of the soul

G4639.gloss: apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)):-- shadow.
G4639.outline:
- shadow
- shade caused by the interception of light
- an image cast by an object and representing the form of that object
- a sketch, outline, adumbration

G4640.gloss: akin to skairo (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus):--leap (for joy).

G4641.gloss: feminine of a compound of «4642» and «2588»; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception:--hardness of heart.

G4642.gloss: from the base of «4628»; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe):--fierce, hard.
G4642.outline:
- hard, harsh, rough, stiff
- of men: metaph. harsh, stern, hard
- of things: violent, rough, offensive, intolerable

G4645.gloss: from «4642»; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn:--harden.
G4645.outline:
- to make hard, harden
- metaph.
- to render obstinate, stubborn
- to be hardened
- to become obstinate or stubborn

G4646.gloss: from the base of «4628»; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse:--crooked, froward, untoward.
G4646.outline:
- crooked, curved
- metaph.
- perverse, wicked
- unfair, surly, froward

G4647.gloss: perhaps from the base of «4628» and «3700»; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability):--thorn.
G4647.outline:
- a pointed piece of wood, a pale, a stake
- a sharp stake, splinter

G4648.gloss: from «4649»; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard:--consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare «3700».
G4648.outline:
- to look at, observe, contemplate
- to mark
- to fix one's eyes upon, direct one's attention to, any one
- to look to, take heed to thyself

G4649.gloss: from skeptomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to «4626» through the idea of concealment; compare «4629»); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal:--mark.
G4649.outline:
- an observer, a watchman
- the distant mark looked at, the goal or end one has in view

G4650.gloss: apparently from the same as «4651» (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal:--disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).
G4650.outline:
- to scatter
- of those who, routed or terror stricken or driven by some other impulses, fly in every direction
- to scatter abroad (what others may collect for themselves), or one dispensing blessings literally

G4651.gloss: probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of «4649» and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting):--scorpion.
G4651.outline: - a scorpion, the name of a little animal, somewhat resembling a lobster, which in warm regions lurk, esp. in stone walls; it has a poisonous sting in its tail

G4652.gloss: from «4655»; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted:--dark, full of darkness.
G4652.outline: - full of darkness, covered with darkness

G4653.outline:
- darkness
- the darkness due to want of light
- metaph. used of ignorance of divine things, and its associated wickedness, and the resultant misery in hell

G4654.outline:
- to cover with darkness, to darken
- to be covered with darkness, be darkened
- of heavenly bodies as deprived of light
- metaph.
- of the eyes
- of the understanding
- of the mind

G4655.gloss: from the base of «4639»; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively):--darkness.
G4655.outline:
- darkness
- of night darkness
- of darkened eyesight or blindness
- metaph.
- of ignorance respecting divine things and human duties, and the accompanying ungodliness and immorality, together with their consequent misery in hell
- persons in whom darkness becomes visible and holds sway

G4656.gloss: from «4655»; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively):--be full of darkness.
G4656.outline:
- to darken, cover with darkness
- metaph. to darken or blind the mind

G4657.gloss: neuter of a presumed derivative of «1519» and «2965» and «906»; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure):--dung.
G4657.outline:
- any refuse, as the excrement of animals, offscourings, rubbish, dregs
- of things worthless and detestable

G4658.gloss: probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage:--Scythian.
G4658.outline:
Scythian = "rude or rough"
- a Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia or modern day Russia
- by the more civilised nations of antiquity the Scythians were regarded as the wildest of barbarians

G4659.gloss: from skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of «3700»; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance:--of a sad countenance.
G4659.outline: - of a sad and gloomy countenance

G4660.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass:--trouble(self).
G4660.outline:
- to skin, flay
- to rend, mangle
- to vex, trouble, annoy
- to give one's self trouble, trouble one's self

G4661.gloss: neuter from «4660»; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty:--spoil.
G4661.outline:
- a (beast's) skin stripped off, a pelt
- the weapons and valuables stripped off from an enemy, spoils

G4662.gloss: from «4663» and a derivative of «977»; worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots:--eaten of worms.

G4663.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm:--worm.
G4663.outline: - a worm, spec. that kind which preys upon dead bodies

G4665.gloss: of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called:--emerald.
G4665.outline: - a transparent precious stone noted especially for its light green colour

G4666.outline: - myrrh, a bitter gum and costly perfume which exudes from a certain tree or shrub in Arabia and Ethiopia, or is obtained by incisions made in the bark: as an antiseptic it was used for embalming

G4667.gloss: the same as «4666»; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor:--Smyrna.
G4667.outline:
Smyrna = "myrrh"
- an Ionian city of Asia Minor, on the Aegean Sea, 40 miles (65 km) north of Ephesus

G4668.outline: - of or belonging to Smyrna, an inhabitant of Smyrna

G4669.gloss: from «4667»; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic):--mingle with myrrh.
G4669.outline:
- to be like myrrh
- to mix and so flavour with myrrh
- wine with myrrh: i.e. wine flavoured with myrrh. The ancients used to infuse myrrh into wine to give it a more agreeable fragrance and flavour

G4670.gloss: plural of Hebrew origin («05467»); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine:--Sodom.
G4670.outline:
Sodom = "burning"
- a city destroyed by the Lord raining fire and brimstone on it
- metaph. Jerusalem Rev. 11:8

G4671.gloss: dative case of «4771»; to thee:--thee, thine own, thou, thy.

G4672.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08010»); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David:--Solomon.
G4672.outline:
Solomon = "peaceful"
- the son of David and was the wisest and richest king that ever lived

G4673.gloss: probably akin to the base of «4987»; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier:--bier.
G4673.outline:
- an urn or receptacle for keeping the bones of the dead
- the funeral couch or bier on which the Jews carried their dead forth to burial

G4675.gloss: genitive case of «4771»; of thee, thy:--X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.

G4676.gloss: of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse):--handkerchief, napkin.
G4676.outline:
- a handkerchief
- a cloth for wiping perspiration from the face and for cleaning the nose and also used in swathing the head of a corpse

G4677.gloss: of Hebrew origin (7799 feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess:--Susanna.
G4677.outline:
Susanna = "a lily"
- one of the women who ministered to Christ

G4678.gloss: from «4680»; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual):--wisdom.
G4678.outline:
- wisdom, broad and full of intelligence; used of the knowledge of very diverse matters
- the wisdom which belongs to men
- spec. the varied knowledge of things human and divine, acquired by acuteness and experience, and summed up in maxims and proverbs
- the science and learning
- the act of interpreting dreams and always giving the sagest advice
- the intelligence evinced in discovering the meaning of some mysterious number or vision
- skill in the management of affairs
- devout and proper prudence in intercourse with men not disciples of Christ, skill and discretion in imparting Christian truth
- the knowledge and practice of the requisites for godly and upright living
- supreme intelligence, such as belongs to God
- to Christ
- the wisdom of God as evinced in forming and executing counsels in the formation and government of the world and the scriptures

G4679.gloss: from «4680»; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error:--cunningly devised, make wise.
G4679.outline:
- to make wise, teach
- to become wise, to have understanding
- to invent, play the sophist
- to devise cleverly or cunningly

G4680.gloss: akin to saphes (clear); wise (in a most general application):--wise. Compare «5429».
G4680.outline:
- wise
- skilled, expert: of artificers
- wise, skilled in letters, cultivated, learned
- of the Greek philosophers and orators
- of Jewish theologians
- of Christian teachers
- forming the best plans and using the best means for their execution

G4681.gloss: probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe:--Spain.
G4681.outline:
Spain = "scarceness"
- the whole peninsula south of the Pyrenees

G4682.gloss: prolongation from spairo (to grasp; apparently strengthened from «4685» through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy:--rend, tear.

G4683.gloss: from sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of «4682» meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom):--wrap in swaddling clothes.
G4683.outline:
- to wrap in swaddling clothes
- of an infant just born

G4684.gloss: from spatale (luxury); to be voluptuous:--live in pleasure, be wanton.
G4684.outline: - to live luxuriously, lead a voluptuous life, (give one's self to pleasure)

G4686.gloss: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of «138» in the sense of its cognate «1507»; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors):--band.
G4686.outline:
- anything rolled into a circle or ball, anything wound, rolled up, folded together
- a military cohort
- the tenth part of legion
- about 600 men i.e. legionaries
- if auxiliaries either 500 or 1000
- a maniple, or the thirtieth part of a legion
- any band, company, or detachment, of soldiers

G4687.gloss: probably strengthened from «4685» (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively):--sow(- er), receive seed.
G4687.outline:
- to sow, scatter, seed
- metaph. of proverbial sayings

G4688.gloss: of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman):--executioner.
G4688.outline:
- a spy, scout
- under the emperors an attendant and member of the body guard, employed as messengers, watchers, and executioners
- the name is transferred to an attendant of Herod Antipas that acted as executioner

G4689.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"):--(be ready to) be offered.
G4689.outline:
- to pour out as a drink offering, make a libation
- in the NT to be offered as a libation
- fig. used of one whose blood is poured out in a violent death for the cause of God

G4690.gloss: from «4687»; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting):--issue, seed.
G4690.outline:
- from which a plant germinates
- the seed i.e. the grain or kernel which contains within itself the germ of the future plants
- of the grains or kernels sown
- metaph. a seed i.e. a residue, or a few survivors reserved as the germ of the next generation (just as seed is kept from the harvest for the sowing)
- the semen virile
- the product of this semen, seed, children, offspring, progeny
- family, tribe, posterity
- whatever possesses vital force or life giving power
- of divine energy of the Holy Spirit operating within the soul by which we are regenerated

G4691.gloss: from «4690» and «3004»; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk):--babbler.
G4691.outline:
- picking up seed
- of birds, esp. of the crow or daw that picks up grain in fields
- metaph.
- lounging about the market place and picking up a substance by whatever may chance to fall from the loads of merchandise
- hence, beggarly, abject, vile, (a parasite)
- getting a living by flattery and bufferoonery
- an empty talker, babbler

G4692.gloss: probably strengthened from «4228»; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly:--(make, with) haste unto.
G4692.outline:
- to haste, make haste
- to desire earnestly

G4693.gloss: neuter of a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort:--cave, den.

G4694.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea:--spot (by confusion with «4696»).
G4694.outline:
- a rock in the sea, ledge, reef
- metaph. of men who by their conduct damage others morally, wreck them as it were

G4695.gloss: from «4696»; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively):--defile, spot.

G4696.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace:--spot.
G4696.outline:
- a spot
- a fault, moral blemish
- of base and gluttonous men

G4697.gloss: middle voice from «4698»; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity:--have (be moved with) compassion.
G4697.outline: - to be moved as to one's bowels, hence to be moved with compassion, have compassion (for the bowels were thought to be the seat of love and pity)

G4698.gloss: probably strengthened from splen (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy:--bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.
G4698.outline:
- bowels, intestines, (the heart, lungs, liver, etc.)
- bowels
- the bowels were regarded as the seat of the more violent passions, such as anger and love; but by the Hebrews as the seat of the tenderer affections, esp. kindness, benevolence, compassion; hence our heart (tender mercies, affections, etc.)
- a heart in which mercy resides

G4700.outline: - ashes: placed on sackcloth as a token of grief

G4701.gloss: from «4687»; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage:--seed.

G4702.gloss: from «4703»; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field:--corn(-field).
G4702.outline:
- fit for sowing, sown
- sown fields, growing crops

G4703.gloss: from «4687»; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown):--seed (X sown).

G4704.gloss: from «4710»; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest:--do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.
G4704.outline:
- to hasten, make haste
- to exert one's self, endeavour, give diligence

G4705.outline:
- active, diligent, zealous, earnest
- very diligent

G4706.gloss: neuter of «4707» as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly:--very diligently.

G4707.gloss: comparative of «4705»; more prompt, more earnest:--more diligent (forward).
G4707.outline:
- active, diligent, zealous, earnest
- very diligent

G4708.gloss: adverb from «4707»; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise:--more carefully.

G4710.gloss: from «4692»; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness:--business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste.
G4710.outline:
- haste, with haste
- earnestness, diligence
- earnestness in accomplishing, promoting, or striving after anything
- to give all diligence, interest one's self most earnestly

G4711.gloss: from «4687» (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle:--basket.
G4711.outline: - a reed basket, (a plaited basket, a lunch basket, hamper)

G4712.gloss: from the base of «2476» (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course:--furlong, race.
G4712.outline:
- a space or distance of about 600 feet (185 m)
- a race course
- place in which contests in running were held, the one who outstripped the rest and reached the goal first, receiving the prize. Courses of this description were found in most of the larger Greek cities, and were like that at Olympia, 600 Greek feet in length

G4713.gloss: from the base of «2476» (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank:--pot.
G4713.outline:
- among the Greeks an earthen jar, into which wine was drawn off for keeping but also used for other purposes
- of the little jar in which the manna was kept, laid up in the ark of the covenant

G4714.gloss: from the base of «2476»; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy:--dissension, insurrection, × standing, uproar.
G4714.outline:
- a standing, station, state
- an insurrection
- strife, insurrection

G4715.gloss: from the base of «2746»; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin:--piece of money.
G4715.outline:
- a stater, a coin
- in the NT a silver stater equal to four Attic or two Alexandrian drachmas, a Jewish shekel

G4716.gloss: from the base of «2476»; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ:--cross.
G4716.outline:
- an upright stake, esp. a pointed one
- a cross
- a well known instrument of most cruel and ignominious punishment, borrowed by the Greeks and Romans from the Phoenicians; to it were affixed among the Romans, down to the time of Constantine the Great, the guiltiest criminals, particularly the basest slaves, robbers, the authors and abetters of insurrections, and occasionally in the provinces, at the arbitrary pleasure of the governors, upright and peaceable men also, and even Roman citizens themselves
- the crucifixion which Christ underwent

G4717.gloss: from «4716»; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness:--crucify.
G4717.outline:
- to stake, drive down stakes
- to fortify with driven stakes, to palisade
- to crucify
- to crucify one
- metaph. to crucify the flesh, destroy its power utterly (the nature of the figure implying that the destruction is attended with intense pain)

G4718.gloss: probably from the base of «4735»; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined):--grapes.

G4719.gloss: from the base of «2476»; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk):--ear (of corn).
G4719.outline: - an ear of corn or of growing grain

G4720.gloss: the same as «4719»; Stachys, a Christian:--Stachys.
G4720.outline:
Stachys = "a head of grain"
- a man with a Greek name, he is said to be one of the seventy disciples, and bishop of Byzantium (Gill)

G4721.gloss: strengthened from a primary tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof:--roof.

G4722.gloss: from «4721»; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently):--(for-)bear, suffer.
G4722.outline:
- deck, thatch, to cover
- to protect or keep by covering, to preserve
- to cover over with silence
- to keep secret
- to hide, conceal
- of the errors and faults of others
- by covering to keep off something which threatens, to bear up against, hold out against, and so endure, bear, forbear

G4723.gloss: a contraction from «4731» (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile":--barren.
G4723.outline:
- hard, stiff
- of men and animals
- barren
- of woman who does not conceive

G4724.gloss: probably strengthened from the base of «2476»; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with):--avoid, withdraw self.
G4724.outline:
- to set, place, set in order, arrange
- to fit out, to prepare, equip
- to prepare one's self, to fit out for one's self
- to fit out for one's own use
- to prepare one's self, to fit out for one's self
- to fit out for one's own use
- arranging, providing for this, etc.
- to bring together, contract, shorten
- to diminish, check, cause to cease
- to cease to exist
- to remove one's self, withdraw one's self, to depart
- to abstain from familiar intercourse with one

G4725.gloss: from the base of «4735»; a wreath for show:--garland.
G4725.outline: - a fillet, a garland, put upon victims

G4727.gloss: from «4728»; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly:--with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.

G4728.gloss: probably from the base of «2476»; narrow (from obstacles standing close about):--strait.

G4729.gloss: from the same as «4730»; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp:--distress, straiten.
G4729.outline:
- to be in a narrow place
- to straiten, compress, cramp, reduce to straits
- to be sorely straitened in spirit

G4730.gloss: from a compound of «4728» and «5561»; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity:--anguish, distress.
G4730.outline:
- narrowness of place, a narrow place
- metaph. dire calamity, extreme affliction

G4731.gloss: from «2476»; stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively):--stedfast, strong, sure.
G4731.outline:
- strong, firm, immovable, solid, hard, rigid
- in a bad sense, cruel, stiff, stubborn, hard
- in a good sense, firm, steadfast

G4732.gloss: from «4731»; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively):--establish, receive strength, make strong.
G4732.outline:
- to make solid, make firm, strengthen, make strong
- of the body of anyone

G4733.outline:
- that which has been made firm
- the firmament, the arch of the sky, which in early times was thought to be solid
- a fortified place
- that which furnishes a foundation
- on which a thing rests firmly, support
- firmness, steadfastness
- metaph. in a military sense: solid front

G4734.gloss: probably contraction for stephanotos (crowned; from «4737»); Stephanas, a Christian:--Stephanas.
G4734.outline:
Stephanas = "crowned"
- a Christian convert of Corinth

G4735.gloss: from an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, «1238»), literally or figuratively:--crown.
G4735.outline:
- a crown
- a mark of royal or (in general) exalted rank
- the wreath or garland which was given as a prize to victors in public games
- metaph. the eternal blessedness which will be given as a prize to the genuine servants of God and Christ: the crown (wreath) which is the reward of the righteousness
- that which is an ornament and honour to one

G4736.gloss: the same as «4735»; Stephanus, a Christian:--Stephen.
G4736.outline:
Stephen = "crowned"
- one of the seven deacons in Jerusalem and the first Christian martyr

G4737.gloss: from «4735»; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively):--crown.
G4737.outline:
- to encircle with a crown, to crown: the victor in a contest
- to adorn, to honour

G4738.gloss: from «2476» (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest:--breast.

G4739.gloss: from the perfect tense of «2476»; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere:--stand (fast).
G4739.outline:
- to stand firm
- to persevere, to persist
- to keep one's standing

G4741.gloss: from a presumed derivative of «2476» (like «4731»); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm:--fix, (e-)stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.
G4741.outline:
- to make stable, place firmly, set fast, fix
- to strengthen, make firm
- to render constant, confirm, one's mind

G4742.gloss: from a primary stizo (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service:--mark.
G4742.outline: - a mark pricked in or branded upon the body. To ancient oriental usage, slaves and soldiers bore the name or the stamp of their master or commander branded or pricked (cut) into their bodies to indicate what master or general they belonged to, and there were even some devotee's who stamped themselves in this way with the token of their gods

G4743.gloss: feminine of «4742»; a point of time, i.e. an instant:--moment.
G4743.outline: - an instant (i.e. a moment) of time

G4744.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. flash intensely:--shining.

G4745.gloss: probably from «2476»; a colonnade or interior piazza:--porch.
G4745.outline:
- a portico, a covered colonnade where people can stand or walk protected from the weather and the heat of the sun
- the portico built by Solomon in the eastern part of the temple (which in the temple's destruction by the Babylonians was left uninjured, and remained down to the time of King Agrippa, to whom the care of the temple was entrusted by the emperor Claudius, and who on account of its antiquity dare not demolish it and build anew.

G4746.gloss: from a primary steibo (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed:--branch.

G4747.gloss: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of «4748»; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively):--element, principle, rudiment.
G4747.outline:
- any first thing, from which the others belonging to some series or composite whole take their rise, an element, first principal
- the letters of the alphabet as the elements of speech, not however the written characters, but the spoken sounds
- the elements from which all things have come, the material causes of the universe
- the heavenly bodies, either as parts of the heavens or (as others think) because in them the elements of man, life and destiny were supposed to reside
- the elements, rudiments, primary and fundamental principles of any art, science, or discipline
- i.e. of mathematics, Euclid's geometry

G4748.gloss: from a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety:--walk (orderly).
G4748.outline:
- to proceed in a row as the march of a soldier, go in order
- metaph. to go on prosperously, to turn out well
- to walk
- to direct one's life, to live

G4749.gloss: from «4724»; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity):--long clothing (garment), (long) robe.
G4749.outline:
- an equipment
- an equipment in clothes, clothing
- spec. a loose outer garment for men extending to the feet, worn by kings, priests, and persons of rank

G4750.gloss: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of «5114»; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon):--edge, face, mouth.
G4750.outline:
- the mouth, as part of the body: of man, of animals, of fish, etc.
- since thoughts of a man's soul find verbal utterance by his mouth, the "heart" or "soul" and the mouth are distinguished
- the edge of a sword

G4751.gloss: from «4750»; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach":--stomach.
G4751.outline:
- the throat
- an opening, orifice, esp. of the stomach
- the stomach

G4752.gloss: from «4754»; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger):--warfare.
G4752.outline:
- an expedition, campaign, military service, warfare
- metaph. Paul likens his contest with the difficulties that oppose him in the discharge of his apostolic duties, as warfare

G4753.gloss: from «4754»; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic):--army, soldier, man of war.
G4753.outline:
- an army
- a band of soldiers
- bodyguard, guards men

G4754.gloss: middle voice from the base of «4756»; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations:--soldier, (go to) war(-fare).
G4754.outline:
- to make a military expedition, to lead soldiers to war or to battle, (spoken of a commander)
- to do military duty, be on active service, be a soldier
- to fight

G4755.gloss: from the base of «4756» and «71» or «2233»; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (praetor), the chief (praefect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens:--captain, magistrate.
G4755.outline:
- the commander of an army
- in the NT a civic commander, a governor
- the name the highest magistrate in the municipia or colonies; they had the power of administering justice in the less important cases
- of civil magistrates
- captain of the temple, i.e. the commander of the Levites who kept guard in and around the temple

G4756.gloss: feminine of a derivative of stratos (an army; from the base of «4766», as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries:--host.
G4756.outline:
- an army, band of soldiers
- in the NT, the hosts of heaven
- troops of angels
- the heavenly bodies, stars of heaven (so called on account of their number and their order)

G4757.gloss: from a presumed derivative of the same as «4756»; a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively):--soldier.
G4757.outline:
- a (common) soldier
- metaph. a champion of the cause of Christ

G4758.gloss: from a compound of the base of «4756» and «3004» (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army:--choose to be a soldier.
G4758.outline:
- to gather (collect) an army, to enlist soldiers
- of the commander

G4759.pos:
1. the commander of a camp and army, a military tribune
  2. Praetorian prefect, commander of the praetorian cohorts, captain of the Roman emperor's body guard
G4759.gloss: from «4760» and «757»; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Praetorian praefect:--captain of the guard.

G4760.gloss: from the base of «4756» and the same as «3977»; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops:--army.
G4760.outline:
- a military camp
- soldiers in camp, an army

G4761.gloss: from a derivative of «4762»; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert:-- wrest.
G4761.outline:
- to twist, turn awry
- to torture, put to the rack
- metaph. to pervert, of one who wrests or tortures language in a false sense

G4762.gloss: strengthened from the base of «5157»; to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively):--convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).
G4762.outline:
- to turn, turn around
- to turn one's self (i.e. to turn the back to one
- of one who no longer cares for another)
- metaph. to turn one's self from one's course of conduct, i.e. to change one's mind

G4763.gloss: from a presumed derivative of «4764»; to be luxurious:--live deliciously.
G4763.outline: - to be wanton, to live luxuriously

G4764.gloss: akin to «4731»; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness):--delicacy.
G4764.outline:
- excessive strength which longs to break forth, over strength
- luxury
- eager desire

G4765.gloss: diminutive of strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow:--sparrow.
G4765.outline: - a little bird, esp. of the sparrow sort, a sparrow

G4766.gloss: (probably akin to «4731» through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch):--make bed, furnish, spread, strew.
G4766.outline:
- to spread
- furnish
- to spread with couches or divans

G4767.gloss: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate); hated, i.e. odious:--hateful.

G4768.gloss: from the same as «4767»; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech):--lower, be sad.
G4768.outline:
- to be sad, sorrowful
- metaph. of the sky covered with clouds
