G4769.gloss: from stuo (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of «2476»); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support:--pillar.
G4769.outline:
- a pillar
- a column
- pillars of fire i.e. flames rising like pillars
- a prop or support

G4770.gloss: from «4745»; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy:--Stoick.
G4770.outline:
Stoics = "of the portico"
- pertaining to the Stoic philosophy, the author of which, Zeno of Citium, taught at Athens

G4771.gloss: the person pronoun of the second person singular; thou:-- thou. See also «4571», «4671», «4675»; and for the plural «5209», «5210», «5213», «5216».

G4772.outline:
- a kinship, relationship
- kindred, relations collectively, family

G4773.gloss: from «4862» and «1085»; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman:--cousin, kin(-sfolk, -sman).
G4773.outline:
- of the same kin, akin to, related by blood
- in a wider sense, of the same nation, a fellow countryman

G4774.gloss: from a compound of «4862» and «1097»; fellow knowledge, i.e. concession:--permission.

G4775.gloss: from «4862» and «2521»; to seat oneself in company with:--sit with.
G4775.outline: - to sit together, to sit with one another

G4776.gloss: from «4862» and «2523»; to give (or take) a seat in company with:--(make) sit (down) together.
G4776.outline:
- to cause to sit down together, place together
- to sit down together

G4777.gloss: from «4862» and «2553»; to suffer hardship in company with:--be partaker of afflictions.
G4777.outline: - to suffer hardship together with one

G4778.gloss: from «4862» and «2558»; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together:--suffer affliction with.
G4778.outline:
- to treat ill with another
- to be ill treated in company with, share persecutions or come into a fellowship of ills

G4779.outline:
- to call together, assemble
- to call together to one's self

G4780.outline: - to cover on all sides, to conceal entirely, to cover up completely

G4781.gloss: from «4862» and «2578»; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict:--bow down.
G4781.outline:
- to bend together, to bend completely
- metaph. to subject one to error and hardness of heart, a figure taken from bowing the back by captives compelled to pass under the yoke

G4782.gloss: from «4862» and «2597»; to descend in company with:--go down with.
G4782.outline:
- to go down with
- of those who descend from a high place to a lower place as from Jerusalem to Caesarea

G4783.gloss: from «4784»; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with:--agreement.
G4783.outline:
- a putting together or joint deposit (of votes)
- hence approval, assent, agreement

G4784.gloss: mid from «4862» and «2698»; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with:--consent.
G4784.outline:
- to deposit together with another
- to deposit one's vote in the urn with another
- to consent to, vote for, agree with

G4785.gloss: from «4862» and a compound of «2596» and «5585»; to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among:--number with.
G4785.outline:
- be depositing a ballot in the urn (i.e. by voting for) to assign one a place among, to vote one a place among
- to vote against with others, i.e. to condemn with others

G4786.gloss: from «4862» and «2767»; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate:--mix with, temper together.
G4786.outline:
- to mix together, commingle
- to unite
- caused the several parts to combine into an organic structure, which is the body
- to unite one thing to another

G4787.gloss: from «4682» and «2795»; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition):--stir up.
G4787.outline:
- to move together with others
- to throw into commotion, excite, stir up

G4788.gloss: from «4862» and «2808»; to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to:--conclude, inclose, shut up.
G4788.outline:
- to shut up together, enclose
- of a shoal of fishes in a net
- to shut up on all sides, shut up completely

G4789.gloss: from «4862» and «2818»; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common:--fellow (joint)-heir, heir together, heir with.
G4789.outline:
- a fellow heir, a joint heir
- one who obtains something assigned to himself with others, a joint participant

G4790.gloss: from «4862» and «2841»; to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in:--communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.
G4790.outline: - to become a partaker together with others, or to have fellowship with a thing

G4791.gloss: from «4862» and «2844»; a co-participant:--companion, partake(-r, -r with).
G4791.outline: - participant with others in anything, joint partner

G4792.gloss: from «4862» and «2865»; to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others:--carry.
G4792.outline:
- to carry or bring together, to collect
- to house crops, gather into granaries
- to carry with others, help in carrying out, the dead to be buried or burned
- to bury

G4793.gloss: from «4862» and «2919»; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance):--compare among (with).
G4793.outline:
- to joint together fitly, compound, combine
- to interpret
- to compare

G4794.gloss: from «4862» and «2955»; to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by:--bow together.
G4794.outline: - to bend completely forwards, to be bowed together

G4795.gloss: from a comparative of «4862» and kureo (to light or happen; from the base of «2962»); concurrence, i.e. accident:--chance.

G4796.gloss: from «4862» and «5463»; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate:--rejoice in (with).
G4796.outline:
- to rejoice with, take part in another's joy
- to rejoice together, to congratulate

G4797.gloss: from «4862» and cheo (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind):--confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.
G4797.outline:
- to pour together, commingle
- to disturb the mind of one, to stir up to tumult or outbreak
- to confound or bewilder

G4798.gloss: from «4862» and «5530»; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common:--have dealings with.
G4798.outline:
- to use with anyone, use jointly
- to associate with, to have dealings with

G4800.gloss: from «4862» and «2198»; to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively):--live with.
G4800.outline:
- to live together with one
- of physical life on earth
- to live a new life in union with Christ, i.e. dedicated to God

G4801.gloss: from «4862» and the base of «2201»; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage):--join together.
G4801.outline:
- to fasten to one yoke, yoke together
- to join together unite
- of the marriage tie

G4802.gloss: from «4862» and «2212»; to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil:--dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).
G4802.outline:
- to seek or examine together
- in the NT to discuss, dispute, question

G4803.gloss: from «4802»; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion:--disputation(-ting), reasoning.

G4804.outline: - a disputer, i.e. a learned disputant, sophist

G4805.gloss: from «4801»; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian:--yokefellow.
G4805.outline:
- yoked together
- of those united by the bond of marriage, relationship, office, labour, study, business, or the like
- of a yoke fellow, consort, comrade, colleague, partner

G4806.gloss: from «4862» and «2227»; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively):--quicken together with.
G4806.outline:
- to make one alive together
- of Christians, with Christ

G4807.gloss: of Hebrew origin («08256») in imitation of «4809»; a sycamore-fig tree:--sycamine tree.
G4807.outline: - sycamine tree, having the form and foliage of the mulberry, but fruit resembling the fig

G4809.gloss: from «4810» and moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree:--sycamore tree. Compare «4807».

G4810.gloss: apparently a primary word; a fig:--fig.
G4810.outline: - a fig, the ripe fruit of a fig tree

G4811.gloss: from a compound of «4810» and a derivative of «5316»; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort):--accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
G4811.outline:
- to accuse wrongfully, to calumniate, to attack by malicious devices
- to exact money wrongfully
- to extort from, defraud

G4812.gloss: from the base of «4813» and (the reduplicated form of) «71»; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce:--spoil.
G4812.outline:
- to carry off booty
- to carry one off as a captive (and slave)
- to lead away from the truth and subject to one's sway

G4813.gloss: from a derivative of sullo (to strip; probably akin to «138»; compare «4661»); to despoil:--rob.

G4814.gloss: from «4862» and «2980»; to talk together, i.e. converse:--commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.

G4815.gloss: from «4862» and «2983»; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid:--catch, conceive, help, take.
G4815.outline:
- to seize, take: one as prisoner
- to conceive, of a woman
- metaph. of lust whose impulses a man indulges
- to seize for one's self
- in a hostile sense, to make (one a permanent) prisoner
- to take hold together with one, to assist, help, to succour

G4816.gloss: from «4862» and «3004» in its original sense; to collect:--gather (together, up).
G4816.outline:
- to gather up
- to collect in order to carry off

G4817.gloss: from «4862» and «3049»; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate:--reason with.
G4817.outline:
- to bring together accounts, reckon up, compute
- to reckon with one's self, to reason

G4818.gloss: from «4862» and «3076»; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone:--be grieved.
G4818.outline:
- to affect with grief together
- give with one's self

G4819.gloss: from «4862» and the base of «939»; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place):--be(-fall), happen (unto).
G4819.outline:
- to walk with the feet near together
- to come together, meet with one
- of things which fall out at the same time, to happen, turn out, come to pass

G4820.gloss: from «4862» and «906»; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack:--confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.
G4820.outline:
- to throw together, to bring together
- to converse
- to bring together in one's mind, confer with one's self
- to come together, meet
- to encounter in a hostile sense
- to fight with one
- to bring together of one's property, to contribute, aid, help

G4821.gloss: from «4862» and «936»; to be co-regent (figuratively):--reign with.
G4821.outline:
- to reign together
- metaph. to possess supreme honour, liberty, blessedness, with one in the kingdom of God

G4822.gloss: from «4862» and bibazo (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of «939»); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach:--compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
G4822.outline:
- to cause to coalesce, to join together, put together
- to unite or knit together: in affection
- to put together in one's mind
- to compare
- to gather, conclude, consider
- to cause a person to unite with one in a conclusion or come to the same opinion, to prove, demonstrate
- to teach, instruct, one

G4823.gloss: from «4862» and «1011»; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine:--consult, (give, take) counsel (together).
G4823.outline:
- to give counsel
- to take counsel with others, take counsel together, to consult, deliberate

G4824.gloss: neuter of a presumed derivative of «4825»; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court:--consultation, counsel, council.
G4824.outline:
- counsel, which is given, taken, entered upon
- consult, deliberate
- a council
- an assembly of counsellors or persons in consultation (the governors and procurators of provinces had a board of assessors or advisers with whom they took council before rendering judgment)

G4825.gloss: from «4862» and «1012»; a consultor, i.e. adviser:--counsellor.

G4826.gloss: from the same as «4613»; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites:--Simeon, Simon.
G4826.outline:
Simon = "harkening"
- the second son of Jacob by Leah
- one of Abraham's descendants
- the one who took the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple
- a teacher at the church of Antioch
- the original name of Peter the apostle

G4827.gloss: from a compound of «4862» and «3129»; a co-learner (of Christianity):--fellow disciple.

G4828.gloss: from «4862» and «3140»; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence:--testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).
G4828.outline: - to bear witness with, bear joint witness

G4829.gloss: middle voice from «4862» and «3307»; to share jointly, i.e. participate in:--be partaker with.
G4829.outline:
- to divide at the same time, divide together
- to assign a portion
- to divide together with one (so that a part comes to me, a part to him)

G4830.outline:
- partaking together with one, a joint partaker
- of something

G4831.gloss: from a presumed compound of «4862» and «3401»; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary:--follower together.

G4832.gloss: from «4862» and «3444»; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar:--conformed to, fashioned like unto.
G4832.outline: - having the same form as another, similar, conformed to

G4833.gloss: from «4832»; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate:--make conformable unto.
G4833.outline: - to be conformed to, receive the same form as

G4834.gloss: from «4835»; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate:--have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
G4834.outline:
- to be affected with the same feeling as another, to sympathise with
- to feel for, have compassion on

G4835.gloss: from «4841»; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative:--having compassion one of another.
G4835.outline: - suffering or feeling the like with another, sympathetic

G4836.gloss: from «4862» and «3854»; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid:--come together, stand with.
G4836.outline:
- to come together
- to come to one's help

G4837.gloss: from «4862» and «3870»; to console jointly:--comfort together.
G4837.outline:
- to call upon or invite or exhort at the same time or together
- to strengthen (comfort) with others

G4838.gloss: from «4862» and «3880»; to take along in company:--take with.
G4838.outline:
- to take along together with
- in the NT to take with one as a companion

G4839.gloss: from «4862» and «3887»; to remain in company, i.e. still live:--continue with.
G4839.outline:
- to abide together with
- to continue to live together

G4840.gloss: from «4862» and «3918»; to be at hand together, i.e. now present:--be here present with.

G4841.gloss: from «4862» and «3958» (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize"):--suffer with.
G4841.outline:
- to suffer or feel pain together
- to suffer evils (troubles, persecutions) in the like manner with another

G4842.gloss: from «4862» and «3992»; to despatch in company:--send with.

G4843.gloss: from «4862» and a compound of «4012» and «2983»; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one:--embrace.
G4843.outline:
- to comprehend at once
- to embrace completely

G4844.gloss: from «4862» and «4095»; to partake a beverage in company:--drink with.

G4845.gloss: from «4862» and «4137»; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete):--(fully) come, fill up.
G4845.outline:
- to fill completely
- of the hold of a ship
- to complete entirely, be fulfilled: of time

G4846.gloss: from «4862» and «4155»; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd:--choke, throng.
G4846.outline:
- to choke utterly
- metaph. the seed of the divine word sown in the mind
- to press round or throng one so as almost to suffocate him

G4847.gloss: from «4862» and «4177»; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian):--fellow- citizen.
G4847.outline:
- possessing the same citizenship with others, a fellow citizen
- of Gentiles as received into communion of the saints
- of the people consecrated to God

Thus Antony made Herod (afterwards king) and Phasael, sons of Antipater, tetrarchs of Palestine. After the death of Herod the Great, his sons, Achelaus styled an ethnarch but Antipas and Philip with the title of tetrarchs, divided and governed the kingdom left by their father.

G5174.gloss: from Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor:--Troas.
G5174.outline:
Troas = "a Trojan"
- a city near Hellespont

G5175.gloss: of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor:--Trogyllium.
G5175.outline:
Trogyllium = "a cache"
- the name of a town and a promontory of Ionia, not far from the island of Samos, at the foot of Mt. Mycale between Ephesus and the mouth of the river Maeander

G5176.gloss: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of «5134» and «5147» through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of «5167» and «5149» through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat:--eat.
G5176.outline:
- to gnaw, crunch, chew raw vegetables or fruits (as nuts, almonds)
- of animals feeding
- of men
- to eat

G5177.gloss: probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of «5088» through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with «1487»), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with «3756», extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were):--be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, × refresh...self, + special. Compare «5180».
G5177.outline:
- to hit the mark
- of one discharging a javelin or arrow
- to reach, attain, obtain, get, become master of
- to happen, chance, fall out
- to specify, to take a case, as for example
- to meet one
- of he who meets one or presents himself unsought, any chance, ordinary, common person
- to chance to be

G5178.gloss: from a derivative of «5180» (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death:--torture.
G5178.outline:
- to beat the drum or timbrel
- to torture with the tympanum, an instrument of punishment

G5179.gloss: from «5180»; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning):--en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.
G5179.outline:
- the mark of a stroke or blow, print
- a figure formed by a blow or impression
- of a figure or image
- of the image of the gods
- form
- the teaching which embodies the sum and substance of religion and represents it to the mind, manner of writing, the contents and form of a letter
- an example
- in the technical sense, the pattern in conformity to which a thing must be made
- in an ethical sense, a dissuasive example, a pattern of warning
- of ruinous events which serve as admonitions or warnings to others
- an example to be imitated
- of men worthy of imitation
- in a doctrinal sense
- of a type i.e. a person or thing prefiguring a future (Messianic) person or thing

G5180.gloss: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from «3817» and «3960», which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or «4141» with the fist (or a hammer), or «4474» with the palm; as well as from «5177», an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience):--beat, smite, strike, wound.
G5180.outline:
- to strike, beat, smite
- with a staff, a whip, the fist, the hand
- of mourners, to smite their breast
- to smite one on whom he inflicts punitive evil
- to smite
- metaph. i.e. to wound, disquiet one's conscience

G5181.gloss: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of «2962»; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian:--Tyrannus.
G5181.outline:
Tyrannus = "sovereign"
- an Ephesian in whose school Paul taught the gospel

G5182.gloss: from turbe (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to «2351»); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb:--trouble.
G5182.outline:
- disturb, trouble
- to be troubled in mind, disquieted

G5183.gloss: from «5184»; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus:--of Tyre.

G5184.gloss: of Hebrew origin («06865»): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine:--Tyre.
G5184.outline:
Tyre = "a rock"
- a Phoenician city on the Mediterranean, very ancient, large, splendid, flourishing in commerce, and powerful by land and sea

G5185.gloss: from, «5187»; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally):--blind.

G5186.gloss: from «5185»; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure:--blind.
G5186.outline:
- to blind, make blind
- in the NT metaph. to blunt the mental discernment, darken the mind

G5187.gloss: from a derivative of «5188»; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit:--high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.
G5187.outline:
- to raise a smoke, to wrap in a mist
- metaph.
- to make proud, puff up with pride, render insolent
- to be puffed up with haughtiness or pride
- to blind with pride or conceit, to render foolish or stupid
- beclouded, besotted

G5188.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame:--smoke.
G5188.outline:
- to cause or emit smoke, raise a smoke
- to smoke

G5189.gloss: from a derivative of «5188»; stormy (as if smoky):--tempestuous.

G5190.gloss: from a derivative of «5177»; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian:--Tychicus.
G5190.outline:
Tychicus = "fateful"
- an Asiatic Christian, friend and companion of the apostle Paul

G5191.outline:
- hyacinth, of the colour of hyacinth
- of a red colour bordering on black

G5192.gloss: of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon:-- jacinth.
G5192.outline: - hyacinth, the name of a flower, also of a precious stone of the same colour, a dark blue verging on black

G5193.outline: - of glass or transparent like glass, glassy

G5194.gloss: perhaps from the same as «5205» (as being transparent like rain); glass:--glass.
G5194.outline:
- any stone transparent like glass
- glass

G5195.gloss: from «5196»; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse:--use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).
G5195.outline:
- to be insolent, to behave insolently, wantonly, outrageously
- to act insolently and shamefully towards one, to treat shamefully
- of one who injures another by speaking evil of him

G5196.gloss: from «5228»; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury:--harm, hurt, reproach.
G5196.outline:
- insolence
- impudence, pride, haughtiness
- a wrong springing from insolence, an injury, affront, insult
- mental injury and wantonness of its infliction being prominent
- injury inflicted by the violence of a tempest

G5197.gloss: from «5195»; an insulter, i.e. maltreater:--despiteful, injurious.
G5197.outline:
- an insolent man
- one who, uplifted with pride, either heaps insulting language upon others or does them some shameful act of wrong

G5198.gloss: from «5199»; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine):--be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).
G5198.outline:
- to be sound, to be well, to be in good health
- metaph.
- of Christians whose opinions are free from any mixture of error
- of one who keeps the graces and is strong

G5199.gloss: from the base of «837»; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine):--sound, whole.
G5199.outline:
- sound
- of a man who is sound in body
- to make one whole i.e. restore him to health
- metaph. teaching which does not deviate from the truth

G5200.gloss: from the base of «5205»; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh):--green.
G5200.outline:
- damp, moist, wet
- full of sap, green

G5201.gloss: from «5204»; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply:--water-pot.
G5201.outline:
- a vessel for holding water
- a water jar, a water pot

G5202.gloss: from a compound of «5204» and a derivative of «4095»; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages:--drink water.
G5202.outline: - to drink water, be a drinker of water

G5203.gloss: from a compound of «5204» and a derivative of «3700» (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical":--have the dropsy.

G5204.gloss: from the base of «5205»; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively:--water.
G5204.outline:
- water
- of water in rivers, in fountains, in pools
- of the water of the deluge
- of water in any of the earth's repositories
- of water as the primary element, out of and through which the world that was before the deluge, arose and was compacted
- of the waves of the sea
- fig. used of many peoples

G5205.gloss: from a primary huo (to rain); rain, especially a shower:--rain.

G5206.gloss: from a presumed compound of «5207» and a derivative of «5087»; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God):--adoption (of children, of sons).
G5206.outline:
- adoption, adoption as sons
- that relationship which God was pleased to establish between himself and the Israelites in preference to all other nations
- the nature and condition of the true disciples in Christ, who by receiving the Spirit of God into their souls become sons of God
- the blessed state looked for in the future life after the visible return of Christ from heaven

G5207.gloss: apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship:--child, foal, son.
G5207.outline:
- a son
- rarely used for the young of animals
- generally used of the offspring of men
- in a restricted sense, the male offspring (one born by a father and of a mother)
- in a wider sense, a descendant, one of the posterity of any one,
- the children of Israel
- sons of Abraham
- used to describe one who depends on another or is his follower
- a pupil
- son of man
- term describing man, carrying the connotation of weakness and mortality
- son of man, symbolically denotes the fifth kingdom in Daniel 7:13 and by this term its humanity is indicated in contrast with the barbarity and ferocity of the four preceding kingdoms (the Babylonian, the Median and the Persian, the Macedonian, and the Roman) typified by the four beasts. In the book of Enoch (2nd Century) it is used of Christ.
- used by Christ himself, doubtless in order that he might intimate his Messiahship and also that he might designate himself as the head of the human family, the man, the one who both furnished the pattern of the perfect man and acted on behalf of all mankind. Christ seems to have preferred this to the other Messianic titles, because by its lowliness it was least suited to foster the expectation of an earthly Messiah in royal splendour.
- son of God
- used to describe Adam (Lk. 3:
-
- used to describe those who are born again (Lk. 20:
- and of angels and of Jesus Christ
- of those whom God esteems as sons, whom he loves, protects and benefits above others
- in the OT used of the Jews
- in the NT of Christians
- those whose character God, as a loving father, shapes by chastisements (Heb. 12:5-
-
- those who revere God as their father, the pious worshippers of God, those who in character and life resemble God, those who are governed by the Spirit of God, repose the same calm and joyful trust in God which children do in their parents (Rom. 8:14, Gal. 3:26 ), and hereafter in the blessedness and glory of the life eternal will openly wear this dignity of the sons of God. Term used preeminently of Jesus Christ, as enjoying the supreme love of God, united to him in affectionate intimacy, privy to his saving councils, obedient to the Father's will in all his acts

G5208.gloss: perhaps akin to «3586»; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel:--matter.
G5208.outline:
- a forest, a wood
- felled wood, fuel

G5209.gloss: accusative case of «5210»; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition):--ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own).

G5210.gloss: irregular plural of «4771»; you (as subjective of verb):--ye (yourselves), you.

G5211.gloss: from Humen (the god of weddings); "hymeneal"; Hymeneus, an opponent of Christianity:--Hymenaeus.
G5211.outline:
Hymenaeus = "belonging to marriage"
- a heretic, one of the opponents of the apostle Paul

G5212.pos:
1. you, yours
    1. to be possessed by you
    2. to be allocated by you
    3. proceeding from you
G5212.gloss: from «5210»; yours, i.e. pertaining to you:--your (own).

G5213.gloss: irregular dative case of «5210»; to (with or by) you:--ye, you, your(-selves).

G5214.gloss: from «5215»; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song:--sing a hymn (praise unto).
G5214.outline:
- to sing the praise of, sing hymns to
- to sing a hymn, to sing
- singing of paschal hymns these were Psalms 113 - 118 and 136, which the Jews called the "great Hallel"

G5215.gloss: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate; probably akin to «103»; compare «05667»); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms):--hymn.
G5215.outline:
- a song in tithe praise of gods, heroes, conquerors
- a sacred song, hymn

G5216.gloss: genitive case of «5210»; of (from or concerning) you:--ye, you, your (own, -selves).

G5217.gloss: from «5259» and «71»; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively:--depart, get hence, go (a-)way.
G5217.outline:
- to lead under, bring under
- to withdraw one's self, to go away, depart

G5218.gloss: from «5219»; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission:--obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing).
G5218.outline:
- obedience, compliance, submission
- obedience rendered to anyone's counsels, an obedience shown in observing the requirements of Christianity

G5219.gloss: from «5259» and «191»; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority:--hearken, be obedient to, obey.
G5219.outline:
- to listen, to harken
- of one who on the knock at the door comes to listen who it is, (the duty of a porter)
- to harken to a command
- to obey, be obedient to, submit to

G5220.gloss: from «5259» and «435»; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman:--which hath an husband.
G5220.outline: - under i.e. subject to a man: married

G5221.gloss: from «5259» and a derivative of «473»; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with:--(go to) meet.
G5221.outline:
- to go to meet, to meet
- in military reference
- of a hostile meeting

G5222.gloss: from «5221»; an encounter or concurrence (with «1519» for infinitive, in order to fall in with):--meeting.

G5223.gloss: from «5225»; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth:--goods, substance.

G5224.gloss: neuter plural of present participle active of «5225» as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions:--goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.

G5225.gloss: from «5259» and «756»; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb):--after, behave, live.
G5225.outline:
- to begin below, to make a beginning
- to begin
- to come forth, hence to be there, be ready, be at hand
- to be

G5226.gloss: from «5259» and eiko (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender:--submit self.
G5226.outline:
- to resist no longer, but to give way, yield (of combatants)
- metaph. to yield to authority and admonition, to submit

G5227.gloss: from «5259» and «1727»; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent:--adversary, against.
G5227.outline:
- opposite to
- set over against: meeting one another
- opposed to, contrary to, an adversary

G5228.gloss: a primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than:--(+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very. In the comparative, it retains many of the above applications.
G5228.outline:
- in behalf of, for the sake of
- over, beyond, more than
- more, beyond, over

G5229.gloss: middle voice from «5228» and «142»; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty:--exalt self, be exalted above measure.
G5229.outline:
- to lift or raise up over some thing
- to lift one's self up, be exalted, be haughty
- to carry one's self haughtily to, behave insolently towards one

G5230.gloss: from «5228» and the base of «188»; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth:--+ pass the flower of (her) age.
G5230.outline:
- beyond the bloom or prime of life
- overripe, plump and ripe, (and so in a greater danger of defilement)
- of a virgin

G5231.gloss: from «5228» and «507»; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank):--far above, over.
G5231.outline:
- above
- above a thing
- of a place
- of rank or power

G5232.gloss: from «5228» and «837»; to increase above ordinary degree:--grow exceedingly.
G5232.outline:
- to increase beyond measure
- to grow exceedingly

G5233.gloss: from «5228» and the base of «939»; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach:--go beyond.
G5233.outline:
- to step over, beyond
- metaph.
- to transgress
- to overstep the proper limits
- trespass, do wrong, sin
- of one who defrauds another in business
- overreaches

G5234.gloss: adverb from present participle active of «5235»; excessively:--beyond measure.

G5235.gloss: from «5228» and «906»; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent):--exceeding, excel, pass.
G5235.outline:
- to surpass in throwing, to throw over or beyond any thing
- to transcend, surpass, exceed, excel
- excelling, exceeding

G5236.gloss: from «5235»; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with «1519» or «2596») pre- eminently:--abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.
G5236.outline:
- a throwing beyond
- metaph.
- superiority, excellence, pre-eminence
- beyond measure, exceedingly, preeminently
- beyond all measure

G5237.gloss: from «5228» and «1492»; to overlook, i.e. not punish:--wink at.
G5237.outline: - to overlook, take no notice of, not attend to

G5238.gloss: from «5228» and the neuter plural of «1565»; above those parts, i.e. still farther:--beyond.
G5238.outline: - beyond: the regions lying beyond the country of one's residence

G5239.gloss: from «5228» and «1614»; to extend inordinately:--stretch beyond.
G5239.outline: - to extend beyond the prescribed bounds, stretch out beyond measure, stretch out overmuch

G5240.gloss: from «5228» and the alternate form of «1632»; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow:--run over.
G5240.outline:
- to pour out beyond measure
- to overflow, run over

G5241.gloss: from «5228» and «1793»; to intercede in behalf of:--make intercession for

G5242.gloss: from «5228» and «2192»; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority:--better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.
G5242.outline:
- to have or hold over one
- to stand out, rise above, overtop
- to be above, be superior in rank, authority, power
- the prominent men, rulers
- to excel, to be superior, better than, to surpass

G5243.outline:
- pride, haughtiness, arrogance
- the character of one who, with a swollen estimate of his own powers or merits, looks down on others and even treats them with insolence and contempt

G5244.gloss: from «5228» and «5316»; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty:--proud.
G5244.outline:
- showing one's self above others, overtopping, conspicuous above others, pre-eminent
- with an overweening estimate of one's means or merits, despising others or even treating them with contempt, haughty

G5245.gloss: from «5228» and «3528»; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory:--more than conquer.
G5245.outline: - to be more than a conqueror, to gain a surpassing victory

G5246.gloss: from «5228» and «3591»; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent:--great swelling.

G5247.gloss: from «5242»; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character):--authority, excellency.

G5248.gloss: from «5228» and «4052»; to super-abound:--abound much more, exceeding.
G5248.outline:
- to abound beyond measure, abound exceedingly
- to overflow, to enjoy abundantly

G5249.gloss: from «5228» and «4057»; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly:--beyond measure.

G5250.gloss: from «5228» and «4121»; to superabound:--be exceeding abundant.
G5250.outline:
- to be exceedingly abundant
- to overflow
- to possess in excess

G5251.gloss: from «5228» and «5312»; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position:--highly exalt.
G5251.outline:
- metaph. to exalt to the highest rank and power, raise to supreme majesty
- to extol most highly
- to be lifted up with pride, exalted beyond measure
- to carry one's self loftily

G5252.gloss: from «5228» and «5426»; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant:--think more highly.
G5252.outline: - to think more highly of one's self than is proper

G5253.gloss: neuter of a derivative of «5228»; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story:--upper chamber (room).
G5253.outline:
- the highest part of the house, the upper rooms or story where the women resided
- a room in the upper part of a house, sometimes built upon the flat roof of the house, whither Orientals were wont to retire in order to sup, meditate, pray

G5254.gloss: from «5259» and «2192»; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience:--suffer.
G5254.outline:
- to hold under, to put under, place underneath
- metaph. to sustain, undergo
- suffer punishment

G5255.gloss: from «5219»; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive:--obedient.

G5256.gloss: from «5257»; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve:--minister (unto), serve.
G5256.outline:
- to act as a rower, to row
- to minister, render services

G5257.gloss: from «5259» and a derivative of eresso (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable):--minister, officer, servant.
G5257.outline:
- servant
- an underrower, subordinate rower
- any one who serves with hands: a servant
- in the NT of the officers and attendants of magistrates as -- of the officer who executes penalties
- of the attendants of a king, servants, retinue, the soldiers of a king, of the attendant of a synagogue
- of any one ministering or rendering service
- any one who aids another in any work
- an assistant
- of the preacher of the gospel

G5258.gloss: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to «5259» through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor:--sleep.

G5259.gloss: a primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)):--among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.

G5260.gloss: from «5259» and «906»; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion:--suborn.
G5260.outline:
- to throw or put under
- to suggest to the mind
- to instruct privately, instigate, to bribe or induce (someone) unlawfully or secretly to perform some misdeed or commit a crime
- to induce (a person esp. a witness) to give false testimony

G5261.gloss: from a compound of «5259» and «1125»; an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively):--example.
G5261.outline:
- a writing copy, including all the letters of the alphabet, given to beginners as an aid in learning to draw them
- an example set before one

G5262.gloss: from «5263»; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration):--en-(ex-)ample, pattern.
G5262.outline:
- a sign suggestive of anything, delineation of a thing, representation, figure, copy
- an example: for imitation
- of the thing to be imitated
- for a warning, of a thing to be shunned

G5263.gloss: from «5259» and «1166»; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish):--show, (fore-)warn.
G5263.outline:
- to show by placing under (i.e. before) the eyes
- to show by words and arguments, i.e. to teach

G5330.outline: - A sect that seems to have started after the Jewish exile. In addition to OT books the Pharisees recognised in oral tradition a standard of belief and life. They sought for distinction and praise by outward observance of external rites and by outward forms of piety, and such as ceremonial washings, fastings, prayers, and alms giving; and, comparatively negligent of genuine piety, they prided themselves on their fancied good works. They held strenuously to a belief in the existence of good and evil angels, and to the expectation of a Messiah; and they cherished the hope that the dead, after a preliminary experience either of reward or of penalty in Hades, would be recalled to life by him, and be requited each according to his individual deeds. In opposition to the usurped dominion of the Herods and the rule of the Romans, they stoutly upheld the theocracy and their country's cause, and possessed great influence with the common people. According to Josephus they numbered more than 6000. They were bitter enemies of Jesus and his cause; and were in turn severely rebuked by him for their avarice, ambition, hollow reliance on outward works, and affection of piety in order to gain popularity.

Paul was brought before Felix at Caesarea. He was remanded in prison, and kept there two years in hopes of extorting money from him. Acts 24:26,27. At the end of that time Porcius Festus was appointed to supersede Felix, who, on his return to Rome, was accused by the Jews in Caesarea, and would have suffered the penalty due to his atrocities had not his brother Pallas prevailed with the emperor Nero to spare him. The wife of Felix was Drusilla, daughter of Herod Agrippa I., who was his third wife and whom he persuaded to leave her husband and marry him.
