G5366.gloss: from «5384» and «696»; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:--covetous.

G5367.gloss: from «5384» and «846»; fond of self, i.e. selfish:--lover of own self.
G5367.outline:
- loving one's self
- too intent on one's interest, selfish

G5368.gloss: from «5384»; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while «25» is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as «2309» and «1014», or as «2372» and «3563» respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness):--kiss, love.
G5368.outline:
- to love
- to approve of
- to like
- sanction
- to treat affectionately or kindly, to welcome, befriend
- to show signs of love
- to kiss
- to be fond of doing
- be wont, use to do

G5369.gloss: from «5384» and «2237»; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous:--lover of pleasure.

G5370.outline:
- a kiss
- the kiss with which, as a sign of fraternal affection, Christians were accustomed to welcome or dismiss their companions in the faith

G5372.gloss: from «5368»; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:--Philetus.
G5372.outline:
Philetus = "beloved"
- a heretic and a disciple of Hymenaeus,

G5374.gloss: from «5375»; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi:--Philippian.
G5374.outline: - a resident of the town of Philippi

G5375.gloss: plural of «5376»; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:--Philippi.
G5375.outline:
Philippi = "Lover of horses"
- a city of Macedonia located on or near the northern coast of the Aegean Sea, between the rivers Strymon and Nestus, and the cities Neapolis and Amphipolis

G5376.gloss: from «5384» and «2462»; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites:--Philip.
G5376.outline:
Philip = "lover of horses"
- an apostle of Christ
- an evangelist and one of the seven deacons of the Jerusalem church
- tetrarch of Trachonitis, was brother to Herod Antipas, by the father's, but not by the mother's side. Philip was born of Cleopatra, of Jerusalem, and Herod of Malthace, a Samaritan: he died in the twentieth year of Tiberias, five years after his mention in Lk. 3:1. He built Caesarea Philippi. His step brother Herod Antipas, married his wife unlawfully. (Gill)
- see 2542, Caesarea Philippi

G5377.gloss: from «5384» and «2316»; fond of God, i.e. pious:--lover of God.

G5378.gloss: from «5384» and «3056»; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:--Philologus.
G5378.outline:
Philologus = "lover of the Word"
- a Christian Paul greets in his epistle to Romans

G5379.outline:
- love of strife, eagerness to contend
- contention
- in a good sense, emulation

G5380.gloss: from «5384» and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to «3534»); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious:--contentious.
G5380.outline:
- fond of strife, contentious
- in a good sense, emulous

G5382.gloss: from «5384» and «3581»; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality.

G5383.gloss: from a compound of «5384» and «4413»; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction:--love to have the preeminence.
G5383.outline: - to aspire to pre-eminence, to desire to be first

G5384.gloss: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):--friend.
G5384.outline:
- friend, to be friendly to one, wish him well
- a friend
- an associate
- he who associates familiarly with one, a companion
- one of the bridegroom's friends who on his behalf asked the hand of the bride and rendered him various services in closing the marriage and celebrating the nuptials

G5385.outline:
- love of wisdom
- used either of zeal for or skill in any art or science, any branch of knowledge. Used once in the NT of the theology, or rather theosophy, of certain Jewish Christian ascetics, which busied itself with refined and speculative enquiries into the nature and classes of angels, into the ritual of the Mosaic law and the regulations of Jewish tradition respecting practical life

G5386.gloss: from «5384» and «4680»; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher":--philosopher.
G5386.outline:
- a philosopher, one given to the pursuit of wisdom or learning
- in a narrower sense, one who investigates and discusses the cause of things and the highest good

G5387.gloss: from «5384» and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian:--kindly affectioned.
G5387.outline:
- the mutual love of parents and children and wives and husbands
- loving affection, prone to love, loving tenderly
- chiefly of the reciprocal tenderness of parents and children

G5388.gloss: from «5384» and «5043»; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal:--love their children.

G5389.gloss: middle voice from a compound of «5384» and «5092»; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something):--labour, strive, study.
G5389.outline:
- to be fond of honour
- to be actuated by love of honour
- from a love of honour to strive to bring something to pass
- to be ambitious
- to strive earnestly, make it one's aim

G5390.gloss: adverb from «5391»; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly:--courteously.

G5391.gloss: from «5384» and «5424»; friendly of mind, i.e. kind:--courteous.

G5392.outline:
- to close the mouth with a muzzle, to muzzle
- metaph.
- to stop the mouth, make speechless, reduce to silence
- to become speechless
- to be kept in check

G5393.gloss: active participle of the base of «5395»; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian:--Phlegon.
G5393.outline:
Phlegon = "burning"
- a resident at Rome greeted by Paul of the book of Romans

G5394.gloss: from «5395»; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion):--set on fire.
G5394.outline:
- to ignite, set on fire
- to burn up
- fig. to operate destructively, have a most pernicious power
- of that in which the destructive influences are kindled

G5395.gloss: from a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze:--flame(-ing).

G5396.gloss: from «5397»; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against.
G5396.outline:
- to utter nonsense, talk idly, prate
- to bring forward idle accusations, make empty charges
- to accuse one falsely with malicious words

G5397.gloss: from phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater:--tattler.
G5397.outline:
- of persons uttering or doing silly things, garrulous, babbling
- of things, foolish, trifling, vain

G5398.outline:
- inspiring fear, terrible, formidable
- affected with fear, timid

G5399.gloss: from «5401»; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere:--be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.
G5399.outline:
- to put to flight by terrifying (to scare away)
- to put to flight, to flee
- to fear, be afraid
- to be struck with fear, to be seized with alarm 1b
- of those startled by strange sights or occurrences 1b
- of those struck with amazement
- to fear, be afraid of one
- to fear (i.e. hesitate) to do something (for fear of harm)
- to reverence, venerate, to treat with deference or reverential obedience

G5400.gloss: neuter of a derivative of «5399»; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent:--fearful sight.
G5400.outline: - that which strikes terror, a terror, (cause of) fright

G5401.gloss: from a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright:--be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.
G5401.outline:
- fear, dread, terror
- that which strikes terror
- reverence for one's husband

G5402.gloss: feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of «5457»); Phoebe, a Christian woman:--Phebe.
G5402.outline:
Phoebe = "radiant"
- a deaconess of the church at Cenchrea, near Corinth

G5403.gloss: from «5404»; palm-country; Phoenice (or Phoenicia), a region of Palestine:--Phenice, Phenicia.
G5403.outline:
Phenicia = "land of palm trees"
- a territory of the province of Syria, situated on the coast of the Mediterranean between the river Eleutherus and the promontory of Carmel, some 30 miles (50 km) long and 3 (5 km) broad

G5405.gloss: probably the same as «5404»; Phoenix, a place in Crete:--Phenice.
G5405.outline:
Phenice = "palm tree"
- the name of a haven in Crete on the south coast

G5406.gloss: from «5408»; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which «443» does not necessarily imply; while «4607» is a special term for a public bandit):--murderer.

G5407.gloss: from «5406»; to be a murderer (of):--kill, do murder, slay.
G5407.outline:
- to kill, slay, murder
- to commit murder

G5408.gloss: from an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder:--murder, + be slain with, slaughter.

G5409.gloss: from «5411»; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment:--bear, wear.
G5409.outline:
- to bear constantly, wear
- of clothing, garments, armour

G5410.gloss: of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with «675»; a station on the Appian road:--forum.
G5410.outline: - Appius Forum, a town in Italy, 43 Roman miles (70 km) from Rome on the Appian Way

G5411.gloss: from «5342»; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas «5056» is usually a general toll on goods or travel):--tribute.
G5411.outline: - tribute, esp. the annual tax levied upon houses, lands, and persons

G5412.gloss: from «5414»; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety):--lade, by heavy laden.
G5412.outline:
- to place a burden upon, to load
- metaph. to load one with a burden (of rites and unwarranted precepts)

G5413.gloss: diminutive of «5414»; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service:--burden.
G5413.outline:
- a burden, load
- of the freight or lading of a ship
- metaph.
- of burdensome rites
- of the obligations Christ lays upon his followers, and styles a "burden" by way of the contrast to the precepts of the Pharisees, the observance of which was most oppressive
- faults of the conscience which oppress the soul

G5414.gloss: from «5342»; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship:--lading.
G5414.outline:
- a load, burden
- of a ship

G5415.gloss: of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian:--Fortunatus.
G5415.outline:
Fortunatus = "well freighted"
- a Christian of Corinth

G5416.gloss: neuter of a derivative from the base of «5417»; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment:--scourge.

G5417.gloss: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment:--scourge.

G5418.gloss: from «5420»; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively):--hedge (+ round about), partition.
G5418.outline:
- a hedge, a fence
- that which separates, prevents two from coming together

G5419.gloss: probably akin to «5420» through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound:-- declare.
G5419.outline:
- to indicate plainly, make known, declare, whether by gesture or by writing or speaking, or in some other ways
- to explain

G5420.gloss: apparently a strengthening form of the base of «5424»; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence):--stop.
G5420.outline:
- to fence in, block up, stop up, close up
- to put to silence

G5421.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison):--well, pit.
G5421.outline:
- a well
- the pit of the abyss (because the nether world is thought to increase in size the further it extends from the surface of the earth and so resemble a cistern, the orifice of which is narrow)

G5422.gloss: from «5423»; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude:--deceive.

G5423.gloss: from «5424» and «539»; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer:--deceiver.

G5424.gloss: probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare «5420»); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties):--understanding.
G5424.outline:
- the midriff or diaphragm, the parts of the heart
- the mind
- the faculty of perceiving and judging

G5425.gloss: apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear):--tremble.
G5425.outline:
- to bristle, stiffen stand up
- to shudder, to be struck with extreme fear, to be horrified

G5426.gloss: from «5424»; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience):--set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.
G5426.outline:
- to have understanding, be wise
- to feel, to think
- to have an opinion of one's self, think of one's self, to be modest, not let one's opinion (though just) of himself exceed the bounds of modesty
- to think or judge what one's opinion is
- to be of the same mind i.e. agreed together, cherish the same views, be harmonious
- to direct one's mind to a thing, to seek, to strive for
- to seek one's interest or advantage
- to be of one's party, side with him (in public affairs)

G5427.gloss: from «5426»; (mental) inclination or purpose:--(be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).
G5427.outline: - what one has in the mind, the thoughts and purposes

G5428.gloss: from «5426»; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight:--prudence, wisdom.
G5428.outline:
- understanding
- knowledge and holy love of the will of God

G5429.gloss: from «5424»; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while «4680» denotes practical skill or acumen; and «4908» indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative):--wise(-r).
G5429.outline:
- intelligent, wise
- prudent, i.e. mindful of one's interests

G5431.gloss: from a derivative of «5424»; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:--be careful.
G5431.outline:
- to think, to be careful
- to be thoughtful or anxious

G5432.gloss: from a compound of «4253» and «3708»; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect:--keep (with a garrison). Compare «5083».
G5432.outline:
- to guard, protect by a military guard, either to prevent hostile invasion, or to keep the inhabitants of a besieged city from flight
- metaph.
- under the control of the Mosaic law, that he might not escape from its power
- to protect by guarding, to keep
- by watching and guarding to preserve one for the attainment of something

G5433.gloss: akin to «1032», «1031»; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult:--rage.
G5433.outline:
- to neigh, stamp the ground, prance, snort
- to be high-spirited
- of horses
- of men
- to take on lofty airs
- behave arrogantly
- to be tumultuous, to rage

G5434.gloss: neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of «5395»); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig:--stick.
G5434.outline:
- a dry stick, a twig
- all dry sticks, bush wood, fire wood, or similar material used as fuel
- of straw, stubble

G5435.gloss: probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor:--Phrygia.
G5435.outline:
Phrygia = "dry, barren"
- a region in Asia Minor bounded by Bithynia, Galatia, Lycaonia, Pisidia, Lydia, Mysia and it contained the cities of Laodicea, Hierapolis, and Colosse

G5436.gloss: probably from «5343»; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian:--Phygellus.
G5436.outline:
Phygellus = "a little fugitive"
- a Christian who was with Paul and deserted him

G5438.gloss: from «5442»; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively:--cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.
G5438.outline:
- guard, watch
- a watching, keeping watch
- to keep watch
- persons keeping watch, a guard, sentinels
- of the place where captives are kept, a prison
- of the time (of night) during which guard was kept, a watch i.e. a period of time during which part of the guard was on duty, and at the end of which others relieved them. As the earlier Greeks divided the night commonly into three parts, so, previous to the exile, the Israelites also had three watches in a night; subsequently, however, after they became subject to the Romans, they adopted the Roman custom of dividing the night into four watches

G5440.gloss: neuter of a derivative of «5442»; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts:-- phylactery.
G5440.outline:
- a fortified place provided with a garrison, a station for a guard or garrison
- a preservative or safeguard , an amulet. The Jews used this word to describe small strips of parchment on which were written the following passages of the law of Moses, Ex. 13:1-10, 11-16; Dt. 6:4-9, 11:13-21, and which, enclosed in small cases, they were accustomed when engaged in prayer to wear fastened by a leather strap to the forehead and to the left arm over against the heart, in order that they might thus be solemnly reminded of the duty of keeping the commands of God in the head and in the heart, according to the directions given in Ex. 13:16, Dt. 6:8, 11:18; These scrolls were thought to have the power, like amulets, to avert various evils and to drive away demons. The Pharisees were accustomed to widen, make broad, their phylacteries, that they might render them more conspicuous and show themselves to be more eager than the majority to be reminded of the law of God.

G5442.gloss: probably from «5443» through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid:--beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare «5083».
G5442.outline:
- to guard
- to watch, keep watch
- to guard or watch, have an eye upon: lest he escape
- to guard a person (or thing) that he may remain safe
- lest he suffer violence, be despoiled, etc. to protect
- to protect one from a person or thing
- to keep from being snatched away, preserve safe and unimpaired
- to guard from being lost or perishing
- to guard one's self from a thing
- to guard i.e. care for, take care not to violate
- to observe
- to observe for one's self something to escape
- to avoid, shun flee from
- to guard for one's self (i.e. for one's safety's sake) so as not to violate, i.e. to keep, observe (the precepts of the Mosaic law)

G5443.gloss: from «5453» (compare «5444»); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan:--kindred, tribe.
G5443.outline:
- a tribe
- in the NT all the persons descending from one of the twelve sons of the patriarch, Jacob
- a nation, people

G5444.gloss: from the same as «5443»; a sprout, i.e. leaf:--leaf.

G5445.gloss: from a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to «5453» through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough:--lump.
G5445.outline:
- any substance mixed with water and kneaded
- a mass, a lump
- of dough
- of clay

G5446.outline:
- produced by nature, inborn
- agreeable to nature
- governed by (the instincts of) nature

G5447.outline: - in a natural manner, by nature, under the guidance of nature: by the aid of the bodily senses

G5448.gloss: from «5449» in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty):--puff up.
G5448.outline:
- to make natural, to cause a thing to pass into nature
- to inflate, blow up, to cause to swell up
- to puff up, make proud
- to be puffed up, to bear one's self loftily, be proud

G5449.gloss: from «5453»; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:--(man-)kind, nature(-al).
G5449.outline:
- nature
- the nature of things, the force, laws, order of nature
- as opposed to what is monstrous, abnormal, perverse
- as opposed what has been produced by the art of man: the natural branches, i.e. branches by the operation of nature
- birth, physical origin
- a mode of feeling and acting which by long habit has become nature
- the sum of innate properties and powers by which one person differs from others, distinctive native peculiarities, natural characteristics: the natural strength, ferocity, and intractability of beasts

G5450.outline: - a puffing up of soul, loftiness, pride

G5451.gloss: from «5452»; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable:--plant.
G5451.outline:
- a planting
- the thing planted, a plant

G5452.gloss: from a derivative of «5453»; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine:--plant.

G5453.gloss: a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively:--spring (up).
G5453.outline:
- to beget, bring forth, produce
- to be born, to spring up, to grow
- to shoot forth, spring up

G5454.gloss: of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place:--hole.
G5454.outline:
- a lurking hole, a burrow
- a lair

G5455.gloss: from «5456»; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation:--call (for), crow, cry.
G5455.outline:
- to sound, emit a sound, to speak
- of a cock: to crow
- of men: to cry, cry out, cry aloud, speak with a loud voice
- to call, to call one's self, either by one's own voice or though another
- to send for, summon
- to call out of (i.e. bid one to quit a place and come to one
- to invite
- to address, accost, call by a name

G5456.gloss: probably akin to «5316» through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language:--noise, sound, voice.
G5456.outline:
- a sound, a tone
- of inanimate things, as musical instruments
- a voice
- of the sound of uttered words
- speech
- of a language, tongue

G5457.gloss: from an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare «5316», «5346»); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative):--fire, light.
G5457.outline:
- light
- the light
- emitted by a lamp
- a heavenly light such as surrounds angels when they appear on earth
- anything emitting light
- a star
- fire because it is light and sheds light
- a lamp or torch
- light, i.e brightness
- of a lamp
- metaph.
- God is light because light has the extremely delicate, subtle, pure, brilliant quality
- of truth and its knowledge, together with the spiritual purity associated with it
- that which is exposed to the view of all, openly, publicly
- reason, mind
- the power of understanding esp. moral and spiritual truth

G5458.gloss: from «5457»; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy:--light.
G5458.outline:
- that which gives light, an illuminator
- of the stars, sun and moon
- light, brightness

G5459.gloss: from «5457» and «5342»; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively):--day star.
G5459.outline:
- light bringing, giving light
- the planet Venus, the morning star, day star
- metaph. Christ

G5460.gloss: from «5457»; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively):--bright, full of light.
G5460.outline:
- light
- composed of light
- of a bright character
- full of light
- well lit

G5461.gloss: from «5457»; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively):--enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
G5461.outline:
- to give light, to shine
- to enlighten, light up, illumine
- to bring to light, render evident
- to cause something to exist and thus come to light and become clear to all
- to enlighten, spiritually, imbue with saving knowledge
- to instruct, to inform, teach
- to give understanding to

G5462.outline:
- the act of enlightening, illumination
- brightness, bright light

G5463.gloss: a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well:--farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.
G5463.outline:
- to rejoice, be glad
- to rejoice exceedingly
- to be well, thrive
- in salutations, hail!
- at the beginning of letters: to give one greeting, salute

G5465.gloss: from the base of «5490»; to lower (as into a void):--let down, strike.
G5465.outline:
- to loosen, slacken, relax
- to let down from a higher place to a lower

G5466.gloss: probably of Hebrew or («03778»); a Chaldoean (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates:--Chaldaean.

G5467.gloss: perhaps from «5465» through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious:--fierce, perilous.
G5467.outline:
- hard to do, to take, to approach
- hard to bear, troublesome, dangerous
- harsh, fierce, savage

G5468.gloss: from a compound of «5469» and the reduplicated form of «71»; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively):--bridle.
G5468.outline:
- to lead by a bridle, to guide
- to bridle, hold in check, restrain

G5469.gloss: from «5465»; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit):--bit, bridle.

G5471.outline: - a worker in copper or iron, a smith

G5472.outline: - chalcedony is a precious stone of misty grey colour, clouded with blue, yellow, or purple

G5473.gloss: diminutive from «5475»; a copper dish:--brazen vessel.

G5474.gloss: neuter of a compound of «5475» and «3030» (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre:--fine brass.
G5474.outline: - some metal like gold if not more precious

G5475.gloss: perhaps from «5465» through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it):--brass, money.
G5475.outline:
- brass
- what is made of brass, money, coins of brass (also of silver and gold)

G5476.gloss: adverb perhaps from the base of «5490» through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate:--on (to) the ground.
G5476.outline:
- on the ground, on the earth
- to the ground

G5477.gloss: of Hebrew origin («03667»); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine:--Chanaan.
G5477.outline:
Canaan = "lowland"
- the land of Canaan
- in a narrower sense: the part of Palestine lying west of the Jordan
- in a wider sense: all of Palestine

G5478.gloss: from «5477»; a Chanaanoean (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine:--of Canaan.
G5478.outline:
- Canaanite, the name of the ancient inhabitants of Palestine before its conquest by the Israelites
- in Christ's time: a Phoenician

G5479.gloss: from «5463»; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight:--gladness, × greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).
G5479.outline:
- joy, gladness
- the joy received from you
- the cause or occasion of joy
- of persons who are one's joy

G5480.gloss: from the same as «5482»; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue):--graven, mark.
G5480.outline:
- a stamp, an imprinted mark
- of the mark stamped on the forehead or the right hand as the badge of the followers of the Antichrist
- the mark branded upon horses
- thing carved, sculpture, graven work
- of idolatrous images

G5481.gloss: from the same as «5482»; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation):--express image.
G5481.outline:
- the instrument used for engraving or carving
- the mark stamped upon that instrument or wrought out on it
- a mark or figure burned in (Lev. 13:
- or stamped on, an impression
- the exact expression (the image) of any person or thing, marked likeness, precise reproduction in every respect, i.e facsimile

G5482.gloss: from charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to «1125» through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege):--trench.
G5482.outline:
- a pale or stake, a palisade
- a palisade or rampart
- pales between which earth, stones, trees, and timbers are heaped and packed together

G5483.gloss: middle voice from «5485»; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue:--deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant.
G5483.outline:
- to do something pleasant or agreeable (to one), to do a favour to, gratify
- to show one's self gracious, kind, benevolent
- to grant forgiveness, to pardon
- to give graciously, give freely, bestow
- to forgive
- graciously to restore one to another
- to preserve for one a person in peril

G5484.gloss: accusative case of «5485» as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of:--be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +...fore, × reproachfully.
G5484.outline:
- in favour of, for the pleasure of
- for, for the sake of
- on this account, for this cause

G5485.gloss: from «5463»; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude):--acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).
G5485.outline:
- grace
- that which affords joy, pleasure, delight, sweetness, charm, loveliness: grace of speech
- good will, loving-kindness, favour
- of the merciful kindness by which God, exerting his holy influence upon souls, turns them to Christ, keeps, strengthens, increases them in Christian faith, knowledge, affection, and kindles them to the exercise of the Christian virtues
- what is due to grace
- the spiritual condition of one governed by the power of divine grace
- the token or proof of grace, benefit
- a gift of grace
- benefit, bounty
- thanks, (for benefits, services, favours), recompense, reward

G5486.gloss: from «5483»; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:--(free) gift.
G5486.outline:
- a favour with which one receives without any merit of his own
- the gift of divine grace
- the gift of faith, knowledge, holiness, virtue
- the economy of divine grace, by which the pardon of sin and eternal salvation is appointed to sinners in consideration of the merits of Christ laid hold of by faith
- grace or gifts denoting extraordinary powers, distinguishing certain Christians and enabling them to serve the church of Christ, the reception of which is due to the power of divine grace operating on their souls by the Holy Spirit

G5487.gloss: from «5485»; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor:--make accepted, be highly favoured.
G5487.outline:
- to make graceful
- charming, lovely, agreeable
- to peruse with grace, compass with favour
- to honour with blessings

G5488.gloss: of Hebrew origin («02771»); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia:--Charran.
G5488.outline:
Haran = "a mountaineer"
- a city in Mesopotamia, of great antiquity and made famous by the defeat of Crassus

G5489.gloss: from the same as «5482»; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over):--paper.

G5490.gloss: from a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval):--gulf.
G5490.outline: - a gaping opening, a chasm, a gulf

G5491.gloss: from a form of the same as «5490»; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water):--lip, shore.
G5491.outline:
- a lip, of the speaking mouth
- metaph. the sea shore

G5492.gloss: from the same as «5494»; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale:--be tossed with tempest.
G5492.outline: - to afflict with a tempest, to toss about upon the waves

G5493.gloss: from the base of «5494» and «4482»; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent:--brook.

G5494.gloss: from a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter:--tempest, foul weather, winter.
G5494.outline:
- winter
- stormy or rainy weather, a tempest
- winter, the winter season

G5495.gloss: perhaps from the base of «5494» in the sense of its congener the base of «5490» (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument):--hand.
G5495.outline:
- by the help or agency of any one, by means of any one
- fig. applied to God symbolising his might, activity, power
- in creating the universe
- in upholding and preserving (God is present protecting and aiding one)
- in punishing
- in determining and controlling the destinies of men

G5496.gloss: from «5497»; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person):--lead by the hand.

G5497.gloss: from «5495» and a reduplicated form of «71»; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person):--some to lead by the hand.

G5498.gloss: neuter of a compound of «5495» and «1125»; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)):--handwriting.
G5498.outline:
- a handwriting, what one has written by his own hand
- a note of hand or writing in which one acknowledges that money has either been deposited with him or lent to him by another, to be returned at the appointed time

G5499.gloss: from «5495» and a derivative of «4160»; manufactured, i.e. of human construction:--made by (make with) hands.
G5499.outline:
- made by the hands i.e the skill of men
- of temples
- of circumcision
- of idols

G5500.gloss: from a comparative of «5495» and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint:--choose, ordain.
G5500.outline:
- to vote by stretching out the hand
- to create or appoint by vote: one to have charge of some office or duty
- to elect, create, appoint

G5501.gloss: irregular comparative of «2556»; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally):--sorer, worse.

G5502.gloss: plural of Hebrew origin («03742»); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim):--cherubims.
G5502.outline: - cherubim, two golden figures of living creatures with two wings; they were fastened to the lid of the ark of the covenant in the holy of holies (both at the sacred tabernacle and of Solomon's temple) in such a manner that their faces were turned towards each other and down towards the lid, which they overshadowed with their expanded wings. Between these figures God was regarded as having fixed his dwelling place.

G5503.gloss: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of «5490» through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively:--widow.
G5503.outline:
- a widow
- metaph. a city stripped of its inhabitants and riches is represented under the figure of a widow

G5504.gloss: of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto:--yesterday.

G5505.outline: - a thousand, the number one thousand

G5506.gloss: from «5507» and «757»; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel:--(chief, high) captain.
G5506.outline:
- a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand soldiers
- the commander of a Roman cohort (a military tribunal)
- any military commander

G5507.gloss: plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand:--thousand.

G5508.gloss: of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean:--Chios.
G5508.outline:
Chios = "snowy"
- is an island in the Aegean, between Samos and Lesbos, not far from the shore of Lydia

G5509.gloss: of foreign origin («03801»); a tunic or shirt:--clothes, coat, garment.
G5509.outline: - a tunic, an undergarment, usually worn next to the skin, a garment, a vestment

G5510.gloss: perhaps akin to the base of «5490» («5465») or «5494» (as descending or empty); snow:--snow.

G5511.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a military cloak:--robe.
G5511.outline:
- a chalamys, an outer garment usually worn over the tunic
- a kind of short cloak worn by soldiers, military officers, magistrates, kings, emperors

G5512.gloss: from a derivative probably of «5491»; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at:--mock.

G5513.outline:
- tepid, lukewarm
- metaph. of the condition of the soul wretchedly fluctuating between a torpor and a fervour of love

G5514.gloss: feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloe, a Christian female:--Chloe.
G5514.outline:
Chloe = "a green herb"
- a Christian woman of Corinth

G5515.gloss: from the same as «5514»; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored:--green, pale.

G5516.pos: 1. six hundred and sixty six, the meaning of which is the basis of much vain speculation
G5516.gloss: the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (4742 as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral:--six hundred threescore and six.

G5517.gloss: from «5522»; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene:--earthy.

G5518.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a choenix or certain dry measure:--measure.
G5518.outline: - a choenix, a dry measure, containing four cotylae or two setarii (less than our quart, one litre) (or as much as would support a man of moderate appetite for a day)

G5520.gloss: from «5521»; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"):--be angry.
G5520.outline:
- to be atrabilious
- to be mad
- to be angry, enraged

G5521.gloss: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.):--gall.
G5521.outline:
- bile, gall
- in the OT used of other bitter things
- wormwood
- possibly myrrh

G5522.gloss: from the base of «5494»; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt:--dust.
G5522.outline:
- earth dug out, an earth heap
- dust

G5523.gloss: of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine:--Chorazin.
G5523.outline:
Chorazin = "a furnace of smoke"
- a town in Galilee

G5524.gloss: from a compound of «5525» and «71»; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish:--give, minister.
G5524.outline:
- to be a chorus leader, lead a chorus
- to furnish the chorus at one's own expense
- to procure and supply all things necessary to fit out a chorus
- to supply, furnish abundantly

G5525.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir":--dancing.
G5525.outline: - a band (of dancers and singers), circular dance, a dance, dancing

G5526.gloss: from «5528»; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance):--feed, fill, satisfy.
G5526.outline:
- to feed with herbs, grass, hay, to fill, satisfy with food, to fatten
- of animals
- to fill or satisfy men
- to fulfil or satisfy the desire of any one

G5527.outline:
- feed, fodder for animals
- food, (vegetable) sustenance, whether for men or flocks

G5528.gloss: apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation:--blade, grass, hay.
G5528.outline:
- the place where grass grows and animals graze
- grass, herbage, hay, provender
- of green grass
- of growing crops

G5529.gloss: of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod:--Chuza.
G5529.outline:
Chuza = "the seer"
- the house steward of Herod Antipas

G5530.gloss: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from «5495», to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner:--entreat, use. Compare «5531»; «5534».
G5530.outline:
- to receive a loan
- borrow
- to take for one's use, to use
- to make use of a thing

G5531.gloss: probably the same as the base of «5530»; to loan:--lend.

G5532.gloss: from the base of «5530» or «5534»; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution:--business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.

G5533.gloss: from a derivative of «5531» and «3781»; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person:--debtor.

G5534.gloss: third person singular of the same as «5530» or «5531» used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be:--ought.

G5535.gloss: from «5532»; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of:--(have) need.
G5535.outline: - to have need of, to be in want of

G5536.gloss: something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price:--money, riches.
G5536.outline:
- a thing, a matter, affair, event, business
- spec. money, riches

G5537.gloss: from «5536»; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of «5530»), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of «5532») to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title:--be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.
G5537.outline:
- to transact business, esp. to manage public affairs
- to advise or consult with one about public affairs
- to make answer to those who ask for advice, present enquiries or requests, etc.
- of judges, magistrates, rulers, kings
- to give a response to those consulting an oracle, to give a divine command or admonition, to teach from heaven
- to be divinely commanded, admonished, instructed
- to be the mouthpiece of divine revelations, to promulgate the commands of God
- to assume or take to one's self a name from one's public business
- to receive a name or title, be called

G5538.gloss: from «5537»; a divine response or revelation:--answer of God.

G5540.gloss: from «5530»; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body):--use.
G5540.outline:
- use
- of the sexual use of a woman

G5541.gloss: middle voice from «5543»; to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently:--be kind.
G5541.outline: - to show one's self mild, to be kind, use kindness

G5542.gloss: from a compound of «5543» and «3004»; fair speech, i.e. plausibility:--good words.
G5542.outline: - fair speaking, the smooth and plausible address which simulates goodness

G5543.gloss: from «5530»; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals):--better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind.
G5543.outline:
- fit, fit for use, useful
- virtuous, good
- manageable
- mild, pleasant (as opp. to harsh, hard sharp, bitter)
- of things: more pleasant, of people, kind, benevolent

G5544.gloss: from «5543»; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor):--gentleness, good(-ness), kindness.

G5545.gloss: from «5548»; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit:--anointing, unction.
G5545.outline: - anything smeared on, unguent, ointment, usually prepared by the Hebrews from oil and aromatic herbs. Anointing was the inaugural ceremony for priests

G5546.gloss: from «5547»; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ:--Christian.

G5547.gloss: from «5548»; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus:--Christ.
G5547.outline:
Christ = "anointed"
- Christ was the Messiah, the Son of God
- anointed

G5548.gloss: probably akin to «5530» through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service:--anoint.
G5548.outline:
- to anoint
- consecrating Jesus to the Messianic office, and furnishing him with the necessary powers for its administration
- enduing Christians with the gifts of the Holy Spirit

G5549.gloss: from «5550»; to take time, i.e. linger:--delay, tarry.

G5550.gloss: of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from «2540», which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from «165», which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay:--+ years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.

G5551.gloss: from a presumed compound of «5550» and the base of «5147»; to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger):--spend time.
G5551.outline: - to wear away time, spend time

G5552.gloss: from «5557»; made of gold:--of gold, golden.
G5552.outline:
- golden
- made of gold
- overlaid or covered with gold

G5553.gloss: diminutive of «5557»; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin:--gold.
G5553.outline:
- gold, both that which lies imbedded in the earth and is dug out of it
- that which has been smelted and wrought
- of a gold coin
- of golden ornaments
- of precious things made of gold

G5554.gloss: from «5557» and «1146»; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry:--with a gold ring.
G5554.outline: - gold ringed, adorned with gold rings

G5555.gloss: from «5557» and «3037»; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite"):--chrysolite.
G5555.outline: - chrysolite is a precious stone of golden colour

G5556.gloss: from «5557» and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase"):--chrysoprase.
G5556.outline: - chrysoprasus is a stone of green colour, inclined to that of gold, from whence it has its name; for this is agate in the breast plate, which was Naphtali's stone. (Gill)

G5557.gloss: perhaps from the base of «5530» (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin:--gold.
G5557.outline:
- precious things made of gold, golden ornaments
- an image made of gold
- stamped gold, gold coin

G5558.gloss: from «5557»; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments:--deck.
G5558.outline:
- to adorn with gold, to gild
- of a woman ornamented with gold so profusely that she seems to be gilded

G5559.gloss: probably akin to the base of «5530» through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin):--body.
G5559.outline: - the surface of the body, the skin

G5560.gloss: apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping:--cripple, halt, lame.
G5560.outline:
- lame
- deprived of a foot, maimed

G5561.gloss: feminine of a derivative of the base of «5490» through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants):--coast, county, fields, ground, land, region. Compare «5117».
G5561.outline:
- the space lying between two places or limits
- a region or country i.e. a tract of land
- the (rural) region surrounding a city or village, the country
- the region with towns and villages which surround a metropolis
- land which is ploughed or cultivated, ground

G5562.gloss: from «5561»; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively):--come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.
G5562.outline:
- to leave space (which may be filled or occupied by another), to make room, give place, yield
- to retire
- metaph. to betake one's self, turn one's self
- to go forward, advance, proceed, succeed
- to have space or room for receiving or holding something

G5563.gloss: from «5561»; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away:--depart, put asunder, separate.
G5563.outline:
- to separate, divide, part, put asunder, to separate one's self from, to depart
- to leave a husband or wife
- of divorce
- to depart, go away

G5564.gloss: diminutive of «5561»; a spot or plot of ground:--field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.
G5564.outline:
- a space, a place, a region, a district
- a piece of ground, a field, land

G5565.gloss: adverb from «5561»; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition):--beside, by itself, without.

G5566.gloss: of Latin origin; the north-west wind:--north west.
G5566.outline:
- the northwest wind
- for the quarter of the heavens from which the wind blows

G5567.gloss: probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare «5597»); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes):--make melody, sing (psalms).
G5567.outline:
- to pluck off, pull out
- to cause to vibrate by touching, to twang
- to touch or strike the chord, to twang the strings of a musical instrument so that they gently vibrate
- to play on a stringed instrument, to play, the harp, etc.
- to sing to the music of the harp
- in the NT to sing a hymn, to celebrate the praises of God in song

G5568.gloss: from «5567»; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms:--psalm. Compare «5603».
G5568.outline:
- a striking, twanging
- of a striking the chords of a musical instrument
- of a pious song, a psalm

G5569.gloss: from «5571» and «80»; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate:--false brethren.
G5569.outline:
- a false brother
- one who ostentatiously professes to be a Christian, but is destitute of Christian knowledge and piety

G5570.gloss: from «5571» and «652»; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher:--false teacher.
G5570.outline: - a false apostle, one who falsely claims to be an ambassador of Christ

G5571.gloss: from «5574»; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked:--false, liar.

G5572.gloss: from «5571» and «1320»; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine:--false teacher.

G5573.gloss: from «5571» and «3004»; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine:--speaking lies.

G5574.gloss: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood:--falsely, lie.
G5574.outline:
- to lie, to speak deliberate falsehoods
- to deceive one by a lie, to lie to

G5575.gloss: from «5571» and a kindred form of «3144»; a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony:--false witness.

G5576.gloss: from «5575»; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence:--be a false witness.
G5576.outline: - to utter falsehoods in giving testimony, to testify falsely, to bear false witness

G5578.gloss: from «5571» and «4396»; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor:--false prophet.
G5578.outline:
- one who, acting the part of a divinely inspired prophet, utters falsehoods under the name of divine prophecies
- a false prophet

G5579.outline:
- a lie
- conscious and intentional falsehood
- in a broad sense, whatever is not what it seems to be
- of perverse, impious, deceitful precepts

G5580.gloss: from «5571» and «5547»; a spurious Messiah:--false Christ.
G5580.outline:
- a false Christ (or Messiah)
- one who falsely lays claim to the name and office of the Messiah

G5581.gloss: from «5571» and «3686»; untruly named:--falsely so called.

G5582.outline:
- a falsehood, a lie
- the perfidy by which a man by sinning breaks faith with God

G5583.outline:
- a liar
- one who breaks faith
- a false and faithless man

G5584.gloss: from the base of «5567» (compare «5586»); to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for:--feel after, handle, touch.
G5584.outline:
- to handle, touch and feel
- metaph. mentally to seek after tokens of a person or a thing

G5585.gloss: from «5586»; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute:--count.
G5585.outline:
- to count with pebbles, to compute, calculate, reckon
- to give one's vote by casting a pebble into the urn
- to decide by voting

G5586.gloss: from the same as «5584»; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote:--stone, voice.
G5586.outline:
- a small worn smooth stone, a pebble
- in the ancient courts of justice the accused were condemned by black pebbles and the acquitted by white
- a vote (on account of the use of pebbles in voting)

G5587.gloss: from a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to «5574»); whispering, i.e. secret detraction:--whispering.
G5587.outline:
- a whispering, i.e. secret slandering
- of the magical murmuring of a charmer of snakes

G5588.gloss: from the same as «5587»; a secret calumniator:--whisperer.

G5589.gloss: diminutive from a derivative of the base of «5567» (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel:--crumb.

G5590.gloss: from «5594»; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from «4151», which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from «2222», which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew «05315», «07307» and «02416»):--heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.
G5590.outline:
- breath
- the breath of life
- the vital force which animates the body and shows itself in breathing 1a
- of animals 1a
- of men
- life
- that in which there is life
- a living being, a living soul
- the soul
- the seat of the feelings, desires, affections, aversions (our heart, soul etc.)
- the (human) soul in so far as it is constituted that by the right use of the aids offered it by God it can attain its highest end and secure eternal blessedness, the soul regarded as a moral being designed for everlasting life
- the soul as an essence which differs from the body and is not dissolved by death (distinguished from other parts of the body)

G5591.gloss: from «5590»; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from «4152», which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from «5446», which is the lower or bestial nature):--natural, sensual.
G5591.outline:
- of or belonging to breath
- having the nature and characteristics of the breath
- the principal of animal life, which men have in common with the brutes
- governed by breath
- the sensuous nature with its subjection to appetite and passion

G5593.outline:
- cold, cool
- of cool water
- metaph.
- cold i.e. sluggish, inert
- in mind: of one destitute of warm Christian faith and the desire for holiness

G5594.gloss: a primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from «4154», which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of «109», which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by  evaporation) to chill (figuratively):--wax cold.
G5594.outline:
- to breathe, blow, cool by blowing
- to be made or grow cool or cold
- metaph. of waning love

G5595.gloss: from the base of «5596»; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish:--(bestow to) feed.
G5595.outline:
- to feed by putting a bit or crumb (of food) into the mouth
- of infants, young animals etc.
- to feed, nourish
- to give a thing to feed someone, feed out to

G5596.gloss: diminutive from a derivative of the base of «5597»; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful:--sop.

G5597.gloss: prolongation from the same base as «5567»; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand):--rub.
G5597.outline: - to rub, to rub to pieces

G5598.gloss: the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality:--Omega.
G5598.outline:
- the last letter in the Greek alphabet
- the last

G5599.gloss: a primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh:--O.

G5600.gloss: the subjunctive of «1510»; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with «1487» and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be:--+ appear, are, (may, might,  should) be, × have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.

G5601.gloss: of Hebrew origin («05744»); Obed, an Israelite:--Obed.
G5601.outline:
Obed = "serving"
- the grandfather of king David

G5602.gloss: from an adverb form of «3592»; in this same spot, i.e. here or hither:--here, hither, (in) this place, there.

G5603.gloss: from «103»; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while «5215» denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and «5568» still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation):--song.

G5604.gloss: akin to «3601»; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth:--pain, sorrow, travail.
G5604.outline:
- the pain of childbirth, travail pain, birth pangs
- intolerable anguish, in reference to the dire calamities precede the advent of the Messiah

G5605.gloss: from «5604»; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively):--travail in (birth).
G5605.outline: - to feel the pains of child birth, to travail

G5606.gloss: perhaps from the alternate of «5342»; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne):--shoulder.

G5607.gloss: present participle of «1510»; being:--be, come, have.

G5608.gloss: middle voice from an apparently primary onos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier «4092»):-- buy.

G5610.gloss: apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively):--day, hour, instant, season, × short, (even-)tide, (high) time.
G5610.outline:
- a certain definite time or season fixed by natural law and returning with the revolving year
- of the seasons of the year, spring, summer, autumn, winter
- the daytime (bounded by the rising and setting of the sun), a day
- a twelfth part of the day-time, an hour, (the twelve hours of the day are reckoned from the rising to the setting of the sun)
- any definite time, point of time, moment

G5611.gloss: from «5610»; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)):--beautiful.
G5611.outline: - blooming, beautiful (used of the human body)

G5612.gloss: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar":--roar.
G5612.outline:
- to roar, to howl (of a lion, wolf, dog, and other beasts)
- of men, to raise a loud and inarticulate cry: either of grief, or of joy
- to sing with a loud voice

G5613.gloss: probably adverb of comparative from «3739»; which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows):--about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, × with all speed.

G5614.gloss: of Hebrew origin (3467 and «04994»); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration:--hosanna.

G5615.gloss: from «5613» and an adverb from «846»; as thus, i.e. in the same way:--even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.

G5616.gloss: from «5613» and «1487»; as if:--about, as (it had been, it were), like (as).
G5616.outline:
- as it were, (had been), as though, as, like as, like
- about, nearly
- before numerals
- before a measure of time

G5617.gloss: of Hebrew origin («01954»); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite:--Osee.
G5617.outline:
Hosea = "salvation"
- the well known Hebrew prophet, son of Beeri and contemporary with Isaiah

G5618.gloss: from «5613» and «4007»; just as, i.e. exactly like:--(even, like) as.

G5619.gloss: from «5618» and «1487»; just as if, i.e. as it were:--as.

G5620.pos:
1. so that, insomuch that
  2. so then, therefore, wherefore
G5620.gloss: from «5613» and «5037»; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow):--(insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore.

G5621.gloss: diminutive of «3775»; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear:--ear.

G5622.gloss: from a derivative of the base of «5624»; usefulness, i.e. benefit:--advantage, profit.

G5623.gloss: from the same as «5622»; to be useful, i.e. to benefit:--advantage, better, prevail, profit.
G5623.outline: - to assist, to be useful or advantageous, to profit

G5624.gloss: from a form of «3786»; helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous:--profit(-able).
